summary: The paper proves modularity of prime-to-3 polarized abelian surfaces over Q with the stated large mod-3 image and local conditions at2 and3, including its quintic genus-two corollary, by a2–3 switch and singular-weight GSp4 classicality. The extraction contains595 items across the complete paper, routes every missing item once, and preserves the mandatory AbelianSurfacesModularity / DESIGN-BCGP25 endpoint over DESIGN-BCGP18 and ACC+ infrastructure. It reuses pending analytic, higher-Hida/Coleman and nonregular-GSp4 proposals and adds completed-category-O and higher-rank ordinary-lifting extensions. Seventy-four source findings include misprints, explicit counterexamples to auxiliary assertions and unresolved proof steps. Complete means extraction and routing coverage; it does not certify the proofs, discharge Arthur’s dependency, or claim Lean formalization.

items.name: Dominant integral tuples
items.statement: For an integer n≥0, Z_+^n is the set of nonincreasing integral n-tuples. These index dominant algebraic GL_n weights; the embedding-indexed tuples used at p are separate copies of this set.
api: conversion to a dominant GL_n character

items.name: Local and global purity
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. A local p-adic representation is pure when its attached Weil–Deligne representation is pure; at residue characteristic p require de Rham first. A number-field representation is pure if pure at every finite place.
api: purity as hypothesis for monodromy uniqueness

items.name: Parabolic weight conventions
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For split reductive G with B,T and standard P=MU_P, use the minimal representatives {}^MW of W_M\W, dot action w·λ=w(λ+ρ)−ρ, and Kostant involution w↦w₀,M w w₀. Write ρ^M for the half sum of roots outside M.

items.name: Positive torus monoids
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For a split p-adic torus with its root characters, T⁺ consists of elements with nonnegative root valuations and T⁺⁺ of strictly positive ones in the contracting directions; use a chosen compact subgroup and valuation lattice.

items.name: GSp4 weight and Borel convention
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. Use the anti-diagonal symplectic form, the lower Siegel parabolic and the upper Borel inside its Levi. Characters are (k₁,k₂;w) with w≡k₁+k₂ mod2. G-dominance means0≥k₁≥k₂ and M-dominance k₁≥k₂. The positive roots are α=(1,−1;0), β=(−2,0;0), γ=(−1,−1;0), δ=(0,−2;0); ρ=(−1,−2;0).
api: Weyl action and Siegel quotient representatives

items.name: Dual-spin dictionary
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. The chosen dual GSp4 identification sends (λ₁,λ₂;w) to exponents (−λ₁−λ₂+w,λ₁−λ₂+w,−λ₁+λ₂+w,λ₁+λ₂+w)/2 in the spin representation. Record μ=(−1/2,−1/2;1/2) and {}^MW={1,s_β,s_βs_α,s_βs_αs_β}.

items.name: Ordinary symplectic representation
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For K/Q_p finite and νρ=ε⁻¹, ordinary means a symplectic stable full flag with ordered diagonal (χ₁,χ₂,ε⁻¹χ₂⁻¹,ε⁻¹χ₁⁻¹). The ordered pair (χ₁,χ₂) is the p-stabilization; p-distinguished means all four diagonal characters are pairwise distinct.

items.name: Semistable ordinary weight2
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. With the preceding ordinary flag, weight2 semistability in this paper requires the entire upper2×2 subrepresentation to be unramified. For residual representations use multiplier ε̄⁻¹; a compatible integral stabilization reduces to the chosen residual ordered pair.

items.name: Ordinary regular GSp4 normalization
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For F⁺ totally real with p completely split, take cuspidal π of GSp4/F⁺ with central character norm² and C-algebraic weight λ=(k_v,l_v;2), using infinitesimal character −λ−ρ. Ordinarity is the Jacquet-character valuation −λ; use the unit-valued normalization χ_λ ρν^(−3/2) abs(ρν^(−3/2))⁻¹.

items.name: Regular GSp4 Galois representation
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real, p split completely in F⁺, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal GSp4/F⁺ representation of weight ((k_v,l_v;2)) and central character norm², with the §1.8.12 geometric-Frobenius normalization. There is a continuous semisimple ρ_{π,p}:G_{F⁺}→GSp4(Q̄_p) with similitude ε⁻¹, unramified at the permitted unramified places.

items.name: Regular local-global compatibility away p
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real, p split completely in F⁺, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal GSp4/F⁺ representation of weight ((k_v,l_v;2)) and central character norm², with the §1.8.12 geometric-Frobenius normalization. For that regular π and every v∤p, WD(ρ_{π,p} at v)^ss is rec_GT(π_v⊗norm(ν)^(−3/2))^ss with geometric Frobenius.

items.name: Irreducible regular purity and monodromy
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real, p split completely in F⁺, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal GSp4/F⁺ representation of weight ((k_v,l_v;2)) and central character norm², with the §1.8.12 geometric-Frobenius normalization. If that ρ_{π,p} is irreducible, it is pure at every finite place and the preceding compatibility upgrades to Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne representations, including the monodromy operator.

items.name: Regular Hodge–Tate weights
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real, p split completely in F⁺, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal GSp4/F⁺ representation of weight ((k_v,l_v;2)) and central character norm², with the §1.8.12 geometric-Frobenius normalization. At v dividing p the Hodge–Tate weights of the regular representation are ((k_v+l_v)/2−1,−(k_v−l_v)/2,(k_v−l_v)/2+1,2−(k_v+l_v)/2), and the representation is de Rham.

items.name: Regular ordinary diagonal
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real, p split completely in F⁺, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal GSp4/F⁺ representation of weight ((k_v,l_v;2)) and central character norm², with the §1.8.12 geometric-Frobenius normalization. For ordinary π, the local upper-triangular diagonal is αε^(1−(k+l)/2), βε^((k−l)/2), β⁻¹ε^(−1−(k−l)/2), α⁻¹ε^((k+l)/2−2), with α,β potentially unramified and specified by the normalized Jacquet character.

items.name: Weight2 automorphic representation
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. Weight2 for GSp4 means C-algebraic weight(1,1;2), a nondegenerate limit of discrete series. It is a singular weight in the paper's convention.

items.name: Ordinary weight2 interpolation
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For F⁺ totally real with p completely split and ordinary cuspidal π of GSp4/F⁺ of weight2 and central norm², interpolation gives a semisimple GSp4-valued ρ_{π,p} with similitude ε⁻¹.

items.name: Weight2 local compatibility
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. The interpolated representation has the stated semisimplified local-global compatibility away p and ordinary local diagonal (α,β,β⁻¹ε⁻¹,α⁻¹ε⁻¹), where α,β are potentially unramified. This statement does not itself assert de Rhamness.

items.name: Pure general-type upgrade
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. If π in Theorem1.8.17 is of general type and ρ_{π,p} is pure, full Frobenius-semisimplified local-global compatibility holds at all v: genericity gives the adjoint L-factor holomorphic at1 and purity determines N.

items.name: RACSDC representation
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. Over a CM field F, RACSDC means regular algebraic, conjugate-self-dual and cuspidal π on GL_n(A_F). Its normalization r_{π,p} uses π⊗norm(det)^((1−n)/2) in local reciprocity.
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Polarized RACSDC Galois system
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For RACSDC π, r_{π,p} is de Rham and has local-global compatibility in the normalized Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne sense; r^c≅r∨ε^(1−n).

items.name: Symplectic GL4 transfer and descent
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For an essentially self-dual cuspidal GL4 representation, retain the symmetric-square versus exterior-square pole dichotomy. In the symplectic case descend to the appropriate GSp4 packet; a general-type GSp4 representation transfers cuspidally to GL4. The orthogonal alternative goes through GSpin4 and is not silently symplectic.

items.name: Stable packet multiplicity
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. In the general-type GSp4 case the relevant packet choices have multiplicity one; algebraicity and the chosen infinity type are preserved by the transfer. Non-general regular cases give reducible Galois representations.

items.name: H1 convention for abelian surfaces
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For a polarized abelian surface A with polarization degree prime to p, use ρ_{A,p}=H¹_et(Ā,Q_p), dual to the Tate module. Its multiplier is ε⁻¹; T_p A⊗Q_p≅ρ_{A,p}⊗ε via the polarization, and its Hodge–Tate weights are0,0,1,1.
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Purity and ordinary reduction of H1
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. The H1 representation is pure at all finite places. Good ordinary reduction at v dividing p makes it crystalline ordinary of weight2 in the paper's convention.

items.name: Isobaric modularity of an abelian surface
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. A/F is modular when there are C-algebraic cuspidal π_i on GL_{n_i}/F, Σn_i=4, for which L(s,H¹(A))=∏L(s,π_i⊗norm(det)^((1−n_i)/2)). A genus-two curve is modular if its Jacobian is.

items.name: Other cohomological L-functions
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For a modular abelian surface, the required low-rank exterior-power functoriality supplies automorphic L-functions for H^i(A)=Λ^iH¹(A). Keep the normalization and the distinction between isobaric and cuspidal transfer.

items.name: Spherical GSp4 Hecke polynomials
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For hyperspecial K_ℓ=GSp4(Z_ℓ), let T_{ℓ,j} be the double cosets of β₀=ℓI, β₁=diag(ℓ,ℓ,1,1), β₂=diag(ℓ²,ℓ,ℓ,1). Define Q_ℓ=X⁴−T₁X³+(ℓT₂+(ℓ³+ℓ)T₀)X²−ℓ³T₀T₁X+ℓ⁶T₀². Define P_ℓ by the source's normalized dual-spin Satake polynomial.
api: evaluation at full Hecke characters including similitude

items.name: Hecke polynomial for H1 normalization
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. For the unramified automorphic Galois representation in §1.8, Q_ℓ is its geometric-Frobenius characteristic polynomial, with the spherical character evaluation understood.

items.name: Hecke polynomial for cohomological dual spin
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. P_ℓ is the geometric-Frobenius characteristic polynomial of ρ_{π,p}∨ε⁻³, not of ρ_{π,p}.

items.name: Finite-coefficient good-reduction cohomology
items.statement: Let K=∏K_ℓ⊂GSp4(A_f) be neat, Sh_K/Q its Siegel threefold, and n≥1. For each ℓ≠p with K_ℓ hyperspecial, G_Qℓ acts unramifiedly on both RΓ(Sh_K,Qbar,Z/p^n) and RΓ_c(Sh_K,Qbar,Z/p^n).

items.name: Eichler–Shimura annihilation
items.statement: Let K=∏K_ℓ⊂GSp4(A_f) be neat, Sh_K/Q its Siegel threefold, and n≥1. For each ℓ≠p with K_ℓ hyperspecial, G_Qℓ acts unramifiedly on both RΓ(Sh_K,Qbar,Z/p^n) and RΓ_c(Sh_K,Qbar,Z/p^n). On both complexes the normalized dual-spin polynomial P_ℓ of equation1.8.27 annihilates geometric Frobenius. The Hecke correspondence is the transpose of the Faltings–Chai convention.

items.name: Arthur dependency registry
items.statement: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6. BCGP25 §1.6 explicitly retains cases of the twisted weighted fundamental lemma as an unproved input. The Atobe–Gan–Ichino–Kaletha–Mínguez–Shin v3 abstract (24 July2026) still states its classification conditionally on that input. The available ordinary fundamental lemma or a special GSp4 case does not discharge the general dependency.

items.name: Modularity theorem for abelian surfaces over Q
items.statement: Use H1, geometric Frobenius and the GSp4 normalization in §1.8. Retain the Arthur input and the source-proof obligations recorded in sourceIssues. Let A/Q have a polarization of degree prime to3. Assume ρ̄_{A,3} surjective onto GSp4(F3), unramified at2 with Frobenius characteristic polynomial different from (X²±X+2)², and good ordinary reduction at3 with distinct Frobenius roots. Then A comes from a weight2 cuspidal GSp4 representation of general type, with a cuspidal GL4 transfer π and L(s,H¹(A))=L(s,π) in the theorem's normalization.
items.locator: Theorem A, §1.1, PDF pp2–3; proved in §9.5 (arXiv v1)

items.name: Holomorphic L-function and functional equation
items.statement: Use H1, geometric Frobenius and the GSp4 normalization in §1.8. Retain the Arthur input and the source-proof obligations recorded in sourceIssues. Let A/Q have a polarization of degree prime to3. Assume ρ̄_{A,3} surjective onto GSp4(F3), unramified at2 with Frobenius characteristic polynomial different from (X²±X+2)², and good ordinary reduction at3 with distinct Frobenius roots. Then L(s,H¹(A)) has holomorphic continuation to C and the expected functional equation.
items.locator: Theorem A, §1.1, PDF pp2–3; proved in §9.5 (arXiv v1)

items.name: Quintic genus-two modularity theorem
items.statement: Use H1, geometric Frobenius and the GSp4 normalization in §1.8. Retain the Arthur input and the source-proof obligations recorded in sourceIssues. Let X/Q be a smooth genus-two curve y²=f(x) with deg f=5. If its mod3 representation is surjective and X has good ordinary reduction at2 and3, then Jac(X) is modular. The rational Weierstrass point makes3-distinguishedness automatic by the F3 enumeration; it is not an omitted arbitrary-surface hypothesis.
items.locator: Theorem B, §1.1, PDF pp3–4; proved in §9.5 (arXiv v1)

items.name: Solid E coefficient category
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. Use solid E-modules, their abelian category, internal Hom and solid tensor. The condensed realization of a topological vector space evaluates on profinite S by continuous maps S→V; complete locally convex spaces give solid objects.
api: topological realization and compactly generated comparison

items.name: Solid Banach space
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. A Banach object is isomorphic to (lim_n ⊕_I O_E/p^n)[1/p] for a set I. It matches the classical nonarchimedean Banach category with continuous linear maps.

items.name: Smith space
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. A Smith object is isomorphic to (∏_I O_E)[1/p]. Its compact lattice and solid topology are part of the datum.

items.name: Banach–Smith duality
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. Internal E-duality sends Banach objects to Smith objects and conversely; it is a contravariant equivalence with evaluation biduality.

items.name: Split exact duality
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. Short exact sequences in the Banach and Smith settings split as used here; consequently the duality is exact. The Smith dual topology agrees with the appropriate compact-open topology.

items.name: Fréchet space
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. A Fréchet object is a countable inverse limit of Banach objects. Comparison with classical Fréchet spaces uses a presentation with dense transition maps.

items.name: LS space
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. An LS object is a sequential colimit of Smith objects with injective transition maps.

items.name: LB space
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. An LB object is a sequential colimit of Banach objects with injective transition maps.
api: continuous factorization through stages when justified

items.name: Fréchet–LS duality
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. Internal duality is an exact contravariant equivalence between Fréchet and LS spaces, compatible with the Banach–Smith stagewise duality.

items.name: Trace-class map
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. For Smith objects V,W, f:V→W is trace class if it is induced by an element of V∨⊗W through evaluation. A map of Banach objects is compact when its dual is trace class.

items.name: Compact-type LS space
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. An LS object is of compact type if it admits a sequential Smith presentation whose transition maps are trace class.

items.name: Compact-type Fréchet space
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. A Fréchet object is of compact type if it admits a Banach inverse system with compact transition maps.

items.name: Compact-type LB space
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. An LB object is of compact type if it admits a Banach colimit presentation with compact injective transitions.

items.name: Compact LB–LS comparison
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. A solid E-module is LB of compact type if and only if it is LS of compact type.

items.name: Flatness of elementary solid spaces
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. Smith, Banach, LB and LS spaces are flat solid E-modules.

items.name: Flatness of compact Fréchet spaces
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. A Fréchet space of compact type is flat over solid E. This does not assert that every Fréchet object has the property.

items.name: Algebraic representation by coaction
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. For an affine algebraic group G/E, an algebraic representation is an O_G-comodule with coassociative counital coaction; keep the discrete vector-space category distinct from analytic representations.
items.note: The right-comodule carrier and bundled category exist at the pin (baseline-comodule). Import the algebraic representation/comodule dictionary and handedness adapter from upstream ReductiveGroups; no new analytic-representation layer owns that algebraic definition.

items.name: Quasi-Stein exhaustion
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. A finite-type adic E-space is quasi-Stein if it has an increasing countable affinoid cover with dense restriction maps on functions.

items.name: Stein exhaustion
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. A quasi-Stein space is Stein if it admits such an exhaustion with each affinoid relatively compact in the next, equivalently its closure there is proper over Spa(E,O_E).

items.name: Analytic representation and distributions
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. For a quasi-Stein analytic group G, define a solid analytic representation by an O_G-coaction; D(G)=Hom(O_G,E) is the convolution algebra dual to multiplication, and a coaction induces a D(G)-module.

items.name: Quasicompact analytic Banach comparison
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. For quasicompact analytic G and Banach V, the source comparison Hom(D(G),V)=O_G⊗V identifies analytic G-representations with Banach D(G)-modules.

items.name: Solid locally profinite representation
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. For locally profinite M, an M-representation is a module over E_solid[M]. For compact M this is the rationalized inverse limit of O_E[M/N]; for general M induce from a compact open subgroup.

items.name: Smooth solid representation
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. V is smooth if colim_N V^N→V is an isomorphism, with N running over compact open subgroups of M.

items.name: Smooth discrete-action comparison
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. The category of smooth solid M-representations agrees with the corresponding smooth subcategory for the discrete group M, with the same fixed-vector condition.

items.name: Enough injectives for smooth representations
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. With the fixed universe bound, the smooth solid representation category is Grothendieck abelian and has enough injectives; generators use compact-open induction of free solid modules on profinite sets.

items.name: Character-smooth representation
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. For a continuous character λ:M→E×, V is λ-smooth if V⊗E(−λ) is smooth. Characters with smooth ratio give equivalent such categories.

items.name: Locally analytic vectors
items.statement: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise. For analytic polydisc subgroups G_r with M_r=G_r(Q_p), define V^{M_r-an}=H⁰(M_r,O_{G_r}⊗V) using diagonal left translation and the given action; V^la is the colimit over r. The right-translation action survives, and V^sm⊆V^la⊆V.

items.name: Arens–Michael completed enveloping algebra
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. Define Û(g)=O_{G,e}∨, the dual of analytic germs at the identity. Equivalently it is lim_{r≥1}U(g)_r for PBW coefficient norms sup_n abs(a_n)r^(Σn_i). The Lie map sends X to differentiation along exp(tX); U(g) has dense image.
api: germ/distribution comparison supplied by the analytic owner

items.name: Cofinal distribution completions
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. The U(g)_r and small-group distribution algebras admit the source's cofinal comparison maps. Û(g) has both compact Banach and trace-class Smith inverse-limit presentations.

items.name: Coadmissible completed-enveloping module
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. A left Û(g)-module is coadmissible if M=lim_r M_r with M_r finite over U(g)_r and U(g)_r⊗_{U(g)_{r+1}}M_{r+1}≅M_r. Use this corrected left-module orientation.

items.name: Coadmissible-to-solid embedding
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. Coadmissible modules embed fully faithfully and exactly in solid Û(g)-modules; their underlying spaces are Fréchet of compact type.

items.name: Admissible analytic module
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. An admissible module is the continuous/solid dual of a coadmissible module, hence an LB space of compact type, with the contragredient action convention.

items.name: Flat enveloping completion
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. The maps U(g)→U(g)_r and U(g)→Û(g) are flat in the source setting, with the corresponding completed comparison used for solid homology.

items.name: Exact coadmissible completion
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. M↦Û(g)⊗_{U(g)}M is exact from finitely generated U(g)-modules to coadmissible Û(g)-modules.

items.name: Exact solid completion
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. The same completion followed by the coadmissible-to-solid embedding is exact into solid Û(g)-modules.

items.name: Algebraic category O
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. For a split Cartan h⊂b⊂g, O(g,b) consists of finitely generated U(g)-modules with locally finite b-action and semisimple h-action.

items.name: Completed category O
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. Ô consists of coadmissible Û(g)-modules with diagonalizable Û(h)-action, finite-dimensional weight spaces and weights in a finite union of translates of the negative-root monoid.

items.name: Schmidt completion equivalence
items.statement: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning. Completion gives O(g,b)≃Ô(g,b), with inverse taking the algebraic direct sum of weight spaces, under the source split reductive hypotheses.

items.name: Chevalley–Eilenberg homology and cohomology
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Define the CE complexes for finite-dimensional Lie algebras and modules with their bracket/action differential and augmentation. They compute derived tensor/Hom by the PBW free resolution; module handedness and the antipode are explicit.

items.name: Solid Lie homology and cohomology
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Use the completed CE resolution and solid derived tensor/Hom for Û(g)-modules. The flat comparison with algebraic U(g) is part of the construction, not a formal identification of ordinary and completed tensors.

items.name: Duality of homology and cohomology
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). RHom(E⊗^L_{U(g)}M,E)≅RHom_{U(g)}(E,RHom(M,E)), with the specified dual Lie action.

items.name: Lie Poincaré duality
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). For dim g=d_g, homology of M[−d_g]⊗Λ^{d_g}g∨ identifies with cohomology of M, including the determinant representation twist.

items.name: Acyclic analytic germ representation
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). The Lie cohomology of O_{G,e} with the translation action is E in degree0 and zero in positive degrees; identify CE with the germ de Rham complex.

items.name: Derived Levi action on nilradical homology
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Construct U(m_w)-actions on derived u_{p_w}-homology/cohomology using a p_w-projective resolution and PBW freeness. The naive CE chain terms need not themselves carry the desired strict Levi action; supply a derived equivariant model.

items.name: Parabolic Harish–Chandra compatibility
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Import the Harish–Chandra centre isomorphism and form Z(g)→Z(m_w). The antipode X↦−X acts on parameters by−w₀; the parabolic projection is compatible with induction and the chosen dot action.

items.name: Casselman–Osborne central action
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). On derived u_{p_w} homology/cohomology, the Z(g)-action induced from M agrees with the action through the parabolic Harish–Chandra map and the specified weight normalization.

items.name: Levi category O finiteness
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). If M∈O(g,b), every H^i(u_{p_w},M) belongs to O(m_w,b_{m_w}); the corresponding homology follows by Lie duality.

items.name: Perfect nilradical complexes
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). The derived u_{p_w} homology and cohomology of an O-module are perfect over U(m_w), using Noetherianity and finite global dimension of the enveloping algebra.

items.name: Parabolic Verma and simple modules
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Write M(g)_λ=U(g)⊗_{U(b)}E_λ and L(g)_λ for its simple quotient; use the analogous Levi objects. Import the ordinary semisimple carrier and full PBW from upstream and add the reductive/parabolic adapters.

items.name: Strict lower-dot orbit
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). W_{<λ} consists of Weyl elements w′ for which λ−w′·λ is a nonzero sum of positive roots with nonnegative integral coefficients.
api: empty-set criterion for antidominant generic parameters

items.name: Verma nilradical homology lies in O
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Assume u_p abelian and w∈{}^MW. For every weight λ, H_i(u_{p_w},M_λ) belongs to the Levi category O.

items.name: Verma homology bound
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Assume u_p abelian, w∈{}^MW and λ∈h∨; then, H_i(u_{p_w},M_λ)=0 for i>d−ℓ(w).

items.name: Top-homology Verma injection
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Assume u_p abelian, w∈{}^MW and λ∈h∨; then there is an injective highest-vector map M(m_w)_{w⁻¹(w·λ+2ρ^M)}→H_{d−ℓ(w)}(u_{p_w},M_λ).

items.name: Lower factors of Verma homology
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). Assume u_p abelian, w∈{}^MW and λ∈h∨; then, lower homology and the top injection's cokernel have Jordan–Hölder factors among L(m_w)_{w⁻¹(w′·λ+2ρ^M)}, w′∈wW_{<λ}. In particular empty W_{<λ} gives concentration and an isomorphism.

items.name: Exponential non-Liouville number
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). x∈E is non-Liouville in this paper if liminf_{r→+∞}abs(x−r)^(1/r)>0. This is the weak exponential lower-bound condition, not Clark's polynomial bound or the stronger all-B exponential condition.
api: equivalent one-B estimate after a finite initial range

items.name: Non-Liouville weight and subcategory
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). λ is non-Liouville if every pairing <λ+ρ,α∨> for α positive is a non-Liouville number. O_nL is the corresponding direct-factor full subcategory of O.

items.name: Completion and derived nilradical homology
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). For M∈O_nL, the canonical map Û(m_w)⊗_{U(m_w)}(E⊗^L_{U(u_{p_w})}M)→E⊗^L_{Û(u_{p_w})}(Û(g)⊗_{U(g)}M) is a quasi-isomorphism. Treat this as a source theorem with the topology proof obligation E011, not as already justified by the false general extension lemma.

items.name: Admissible dual cohomology
items.statement: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M). For M∈O_nL and every i, H^i(u_{p_w},M̂∨) identifies with the dual of the completed algebraic H_i(u_{p_w},M), hence is admissible over Û(m_w). This inherits the comparison proof obligation.

items.name: Z-solid analytification of algebraic schemes
items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. Associate AnSpec(A,Mod(A)) to an affine E-scheme using A-modules solid over Z and glue. A principal Zariski open A[1/f] becomes a proper closed immersion in this analytic-stack construction; its complement is the derived f-complete formal piece.

items.name: Formal analytic Bruhat cell
items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. Give the Schubert variety X_w its analytic formal-completion neighborhood X′_w, and define C′_w=X′_w minus the union of X′_{w′} for STRICT w′<w. This corrects the empty-cell typo.

items.name: Polynomial/formal coordinates of a cell
items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. C′_w has polynomial variables for roots in w⁻¹Φ⁻∩Φ⁺ and formal variables for roots in w⁻¹Φ⁻∩Φ⁻, with derived completeness in the latter. The formal identity group Ĝ acts through the Z-solid analytic stack.

items.name: Formal group representations and Lie modules
items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. Representations of Ĝ in the indicated solid category are equivalent to U(g)-modules on solid E-vector spaces, by compatible jets and differentiation.

items.name: Root-group compact cohomology
items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. For a root group U_α, RΓ_c(U_α,O)=E[T_α], and its derived u_α-homology is E(α)[1].

items.name: Formal-root compact cohomology
items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. For the formal root group Û_α, RΓ_c(Û_α,O)=E[T_α,T_α⁻¹]/E[T_α][−1], and derived u_α-homology is E(−α)[−1].

items.name: Formal Bruhat stabilizer quotient
items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. The stabilizer of w for Ĝ⋊B is (B∩B_w)^∧\((B̂_w×B̂)⋊(B∩B_w)), with maps (b,b′,b″)↦(b(b′)⁻¹,b′b″) and b↦(b⁻¹,b⁻¹,b) as in the source. Keep the embeddings, not just an abstract group isomorphism.

items.name: Equivariant trivialization on a cell
items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. items.statement: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group. If ℓ(s_βw)=ℓ(w)+1 and that coroot pairing is not a positive integer, M^w_λ→M^{s_βw}_λ is an isomorphism. It is obtained from the sl2 intertwiner tensored with the partial-cell compact cohomology.

items.name: Natural weight topology
items.statement: Use finite-dimensional weight spaces with chosen bases for O-modules, and PBW multiindices (not adjoint weight spaces) for U(g). items.name: Banach sheaf
items.statement: Let C/E be a complete rank-one valued extension, X an adic space locally of finite type over C, G a split reductive analytic group, P a parabolic, and FL=P\G. items.statement: Let C/E be a complete rank-one valued extension, X an adic space locally of finite type over C, G a split reductive analytic group, P a parabolic, and FL=P\G. Define LB_(g,Q)(C_{w,Q}†) using ambient neighborhoods and compatible Banach systems with G_r⋊Q_s actions, not just an abstract Q-action on the underlying topological stratum.

items.name: Dagger stabilizer quotient
items.statement: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions. The orbit stabilizer has identity germ P_{w,e}×Q_e and quotient (P_w∩Q)_e\((P_{w,e}×Q_e)⋊(P_w∩Q)); derive its maps from (g,q) with gq∈P_w.

items.name: Three-action stabilizer description
items.statement: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions. A stabilizer representation is equivalently a space with compatible commuting P_{w,e},Q_e actions and an adjoint P_w∩Q action, agreeing on the embedded intersection germ.

items.name: Finite-level orbit stabilizers
items.statement: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions. Construct the radius-dependent stabilizer groups Stab(w)_{r,s} with their quotient maps and cofinality, so Banach stages carry actual analytic actions before taking germs.

items.name: LB stabilizer representation
items.statement: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions. An LB stabilizer representation V=colim_rV_r has an action of Stab(w), analytic Stab(w)_{r,s} actions on each V_r for suitable s, compatible transition maps, and the prescribed identity-germ/intersection action on the colimit.

items.name: Dagger orbit fibre equivalence
items.statement: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions. Taking the fibre at w gives an equivalence between LB_(g,Q)(C_{w,Q}†) and LB representations of the indicated stabilizer; the inverse is analytic induction on the orbit germ.

items.name: Restriction through fibre equivalences
items.statement: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions. Restriction from homogeneous (g,G)-sheaves to the dagger Q-orbit agrees with restriction along the explicit stabilizer embedding; the Q_e action is the difference of the Q and g actions.

items.name: Orbit nilradical and centre comparison
items.statement: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions. Moving-u_P-annihilated orbit sheaves correspond to stabilizer representations trivial on U_{P_w,e}; the horizontal centre agrees with the conjugated Levi-centre action specified by w.

items.name: Character twist on an orbit
items.statement: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions. Twisting the Q-linearization by a character gives the corresponding stabilizer-character twist under the fibre equivalence, without inventing a g-character on all of g.

items.name: Integrable LB Lie representation
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. An LB g-representation has an injective Banach filtration integrating to shrinking G_r, with compatible subgroup restriction maps and the given differentiated action.

items.name: Exact dual completion functor
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. M↦M̂∨ is exact and contravariant from algebraic category O to integrable LB g-representations; for a Verma module the dual is the source analytic induced-function representation.

items.name: Algebraic coset of parabolic weights
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. M is λ-algebraic when each weight ν satisfies ν−λ∈X*(T), with λ extending to the stated Levi/Q character. This integrality is required to integrate the twisted q-action.

items.name: Integration of the twisted parabolic action
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. For M in the stated λ-algebraic parabolic O, the q-action on M(−λ) integrates to Q. Use nilpotence on root groups and torus-integrality descent; do not assert a general equivalence between Lie representations and representations of every nonsimply-connected semisimple group.

items.name: Levi orbit parabolic
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. Q_{M_w}=(P_w∩Q)/(U_{P_w}∩Q) is the parabolic in M_w containing the indicated Borel, for the orbit representative w used in the source.

items.name: Admissible Levi representation with character shift
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. Adm(m_w,Q_{M_w})^λ consists of admissible Û(m_w)-modules with compatible Q_{M_w}-action, locally analytic on a uniform small subgroup at Banach stages, whose derivative is λ plus the m_w-action.
api: twisting λ by an algebraic character

items.name: Uniqueness of integrated action
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. On the connected parabolic in this admissible setting, the compatible algebraic/analytic action is determined by the infinitesimal action and the required integral-character data.

items.name: Admissible-to-stabilizer embedding
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. The admissible Levi category embeds fully faithfully into the LB stabilizer category, with U_{P_w,e} trivial and Q_e factoring through the specified abelian quotient via λ.

items.name: Parabolic O to admissible representations
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. M↦M̂∨(λ), with Q-action integrated from M(−λ), is exact contravariant and fully faithful from λ-algebraic parabolic O into Adm(m_w,Q_{M_w})^λ.

items.name: Algebraic shift comparison
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. Changing λ by an algebraic character μ and twisting the module accordingly gives canonically compatible admissible/stabilizer representations; the transition preserves the differentiated-action convention.

items.name: Higher Coleman coefficient sheaf functor
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. HCS_{Q,w,λ} is the composite of dual completion, the admissible-to-stabilizer embedding and the orbit fibre equivalence. It is an exact contravariant functor from λ-algebraic Levi parabolic O to LB_(g,Q)(C_{w,Q}†).

items.name: HCS twisting
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. HCS intertwines algebraic shifts of λ and the corresponding Q-character twists, with the source sign convention.

items.name: HCS central action
items.statement: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters. For z∈Z(m_w), HCS(z)=Θ_hor(ι(wz)), where the antipode and conjugation by w are retained.

items.name: Analytic localization functor
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. Define Loc(M)=RHom_{g,star2}(M,Cla), valued in solid O_FL-sheaf complexes with the remaining group/Lie actions.
api: central action and restriction to dagger cells

items.name: Localization through completion and dual
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. Loc(M)≅RHom_{g,star2}(M̂,Cla)≅RHom_{g,star2}(E,M̂∨⊗Cla). The free case is analytic germ acyclicity and the general case uses a finite free resolution.

items.name: Central character of localization
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. For z∈Z(g), Loc(z)=Θ_hor(HC(ιz)).

items.name: Finite central algebra acting on localization
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. If M has infinitesimal character λ modulo dot-W action, the horizontal Z(m)-action on Loc(M) factors through Z(m)⊗_{HC,Z(g)}(−w₀λ).

items.name: Correct singular central-block decomposition
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. Decompose this finite central algebra by DISTINCT characters among −w₀,M(w·λ+2ρ^M), w∈{}^MW. Equal characters at a singular weight form one nonreduced block; they must not be repeated as independent idempotents.

items.name: Dual localization formula
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. RHom_{O_FL}(Loc(M),O_FL)≅D̃^la⊗^L_{U(g)}M, with the correct left/right actions and CE comparison.

items.name: B-equivariance of localization
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. For λ-algebraic M, twisting by−λ means the integrated B-linearization on the source module; retain its original g-module action. Construct the resulting B-equivariant localization.

items.name: Localization and algebraic nilradical homology
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. If λ is non-Liouville and M is λ-algebraic in O, H^i(Loc(M(−λ))) on C_w† is HCS_{w,λ}(H_i(u_{p_w},M)), with the source conjugate-Levi actions. This theorem inherits the non-Liouville completion proof obligation.

items.name: Germ Shapiro comparison
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. RHom_g(M(−λ),O_{U_{P_w}\G,e})≅RHom_{u_{p_w}}(E,M̂∨(λ)), through the two germ-acyclicity and flat Smith-colimit comparisons. Cohomology and fibre commute only with the supplied LB/CE hypotheses.

items.name: Kostant homology
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. For a finite-dimensional irreducible highest-weight representation V_λ with dominant algebraic λ, H_i(u_p,V_λ)=⊕_{w∈{}^MW,ℓ(w)=d−i}L_{w·λ+2ρ^M}. Import the upstream finite-dimensional representation theory, then prove this nilradical-homology refinement.

items.name: Localization of finite-dimensional representations
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. Loc(V_λ) is the direct sum over w∈{}^MW of the coherent homogeneous bundle L_{−w₀,M(w·λ+2ρ^M)}[−d+ℓ(w)], with the source action conventions.

items.name: Admissible cohomology for Verma localization
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. If λ is non-Liouville and u_{P_w} abelian, every H^i(Loc(M_λ(−λ))) on C_w† is in the image of HCS_{w,λ}.

items.name: Non-Liouville Verma localization bound
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. If λ∈X*(T)⊗E is non-Liouville and u_{P_w} is abelian, the cohomology vanishes for i>d−ℓ(w).

items.name: Highest-weight quotient of Verma localization
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. If λ∈X*(T)⊗E is non-Liouville and u_{P_w} is abelian, there is a surjection H^{d−ℓ(w)}Loc(M_λ(−λ)) on C_w†→HCS_{w,λ}(M(m_w)_{λ+w⁻¹w₀,Mρ+ρ}).

items.name: Lower localization factors
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. If λ∈X*(T)⊗E is non-Liouville and u_{P_w} is abelian, the highest-weight kernel and all lower cohomology have finite filtrations with factors L_{w,−w₀,M(w′·λ+2ρ^M)}⊗E(λ−w⁻¹w′·λ−w⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ), w′∈wW_{<λ}.

items.name: Unconditional Verma localization amplitude
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. For arbitrary λ, without non-Liouville assumption, Loc(M_λ(−λ)) on C_w† is concentrated in degrees0,…,d−ℓ(w). This uses the direct germ computation rather than the completion comparison.

items.name: Unconditional highest-weight quotient
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. For arbitrary λ there is the same highest-weight surjection as in3.5.20, and it is an isomorphism for w=w₀^M.

items.name: Direct Verma germ cohomology
items.statement: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor. Ext^i_{b,star2}(E(λ),O_{U_{P_w}\G,e}) vanishes outside0,…,d−ℓ(w), and its top degree surjects onto M̂(m_w)_{λ+w⁻¹w₀,Mρ+ρ}∨; at w=w₀^M this is an isomorphism. The completion hat corrects the printed target.

items.name: Two-cell singular orbit geometry
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. Construct the map C_{w₃,Q}→P1, identify C_{w₂} with the fibre at∞, C_{w₃} with the A1 preimage, and C_{w₃}∩C_{w₃}s_β with the G_m preimage. The translate C_{w₃}s_β is not the closed cell C_{w₃s_β}.

items.name: Klingen-to-Bruhat coefficient comparison
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. Conjugation by s_β identifies the indicated parabolic-O categories and compares restrictions of HCS_{Q,w₃,η} to the two Bruhat cells, with the stated algebraic twists.

items.name: Coefficient extension across the closed cell
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. The open-extension/whole-orbit/closed-restriction sequence for the Klingen HCS sheaf gives the exact sheaf extension used to define the Cousin boundary, retaining the η and λ−η twists.

items.name: Singular localization triangle
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. The localization on the two-cell orbit sits in the exact triangle whose open term is the w₃ HCS sheaf and whose closed term is the w₂ HCS sheaf shifted[−1], with the source twists. The horizontal μ action has the common scalar μ₀ on the graded terms.

items.name: Derived Cartan invariants
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. Take derived invariants for Θ_hor(μ)−μ₀ in the localization triangle. Its H¹ yields an extension of the two coefficient sheaves; the construction retains the off-diagonal central action.

items.name: Cartan extension equals geometric extension
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. The H¹ Cartan-invariant extension agrees, up to a nonzero scalar and the B-twist λ−η, with the geometric extension3.6.5. The source proof depends on the unresolved fibre calculation in3.6.15.

items.name: Reduction to a two-dimensional Lie complex
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. The h′=kerβ and u_Q partial cohomology lies in degree0 for the module used here; the remaining computation is the CE complex for EX_β⊕EH_β in degrees0,1,2.

items.name: Comparison map into Cartan H1
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. Using s_βλ−β=λ, send a section s of the translated HCS sheaf twisted by−β to the cocycle(s,0) in the two-dimensional Lie complex. Verify the differential and equivariance before passing to H¹.

items.name: Scalar endomorphisms on the overlap
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. On C_{w₃}†∩C_{w₃}†s_β, the two sides of3.6.13 are isomorphic and their endomorphism algebra in the stated equivariant LB category is E.

items.name: Scalar endomorphisms on the closed cell
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. The same isomorphism and scalar-endomorphism assertion hold on C_{w₂}†, using the stabilizer/Verma calculation.

items.name: Nonvanishing comparison target
items.statement: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell. The map3.6.13 is asserted to be an isomorphism by proving it nonzero on the overlap and closed fibres. The closed-fibre operator x∂+1 is injective on germs; the printed overlap operator(x+1)∂+1 has ambient kernel1/(1+x). A proof on the actual constrained fibre, or a different nonvanishing argument, remains required.

items.name: Compatible compactified towers
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. Construct the finite and infinite p-level toroidal/minimal towers, transition maps, boundary ideal I and Hodge–Tate period map π_HT, with Hecke actions and the morphism to the minimal compactification.

items.name: Smooth structure sheaf on the tower
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. O^sm is the sheaf of smooth vectors in O_Sh for the level-group action; define I^sm similarly for the boundary ideal.

items.name: Finite-level description of smooth functions
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. The filtered colimit of pullbacks of finite-level analytic structure sheaves is O^sm on the infinite-level toroidal tower.

items.name: Boundary ideals and smooth vectors
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. The analogous finite-level colimit of boundary ideals identifies with I^sm; pullback and multiplication agree with the inclusion in O^sm.

items.name: Primitive completed-cohomology comparison
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. The completed étale cohomology complex tensored with C_p agrees with analytic cohomology of O_Sh on the infinite-level toroidal tower, with Galois and level actions and the primitive-comparison hypotheses of §4.4.

items.name: Primitive compact-support comparison
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary.
