The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. The corresponding compactly supported completed complex compares with the boundary-ideal coefficient complex. This comparison uses toroidal boundary geometry, not a declaration that every nonproper primitive comparison is automatic.

items.name: Derived Hodge–Tate coefficient functor
items.statement: On a chosen Hodge–Tate flag neighborhood U_FL and compatible toroidal preimage U, define VB_Σ(F)=colim_{K′_p}RΓ(K′_p,π_HT,Σ⁻¹F⊗^L_{π_HT,Σ⁻¹O_FL}O_U), taking sufficiently small analytic subgroups whose Lie actions integrate on the Banach stages. VB_Σ⁰ is its degree-zero functor; the output is an O_U^sm-module complex. Glue under compatible cone refinements to define VB.

items.name: Arithmetic Sen descent for coefficients
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. On a sufficiently small toric chart, construct the cyclotomic Sen module over the decompleted coefficient algebra and recover the C_p coefficient module by base change; the Lie action of Γ acts on B_∞, not on its fixed subalgebra B.

items.name: Algebraic bundles under VB
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. For a finite-dimensional algebraic Levi representation L_κ, VB^0(L_κ) identifies with the classical smooth automorphic bundle with the μ-weight Tate normalization κ(μ). Distinguish this normalization from the untwisted coherent bundle used in §4.8.

items.name: Reduced Hodge–Tate functor
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. Define VB_red(F)=VB(F)⊗^L_{VB(O_FL)}O^sm[0], using the augmentation of the derived logarithmic comparison algebra.
api: comparison with VB^0 on acyclic coefficients

items.name: Exact global coefficient descent
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. VB^0 is exact on compatible (g,G)-equivariant LB sheaves annihilated by the moving nilradical.

items.name: Uniform finite-level Banach presentations
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. Locally VB^0(F) is a filtered union of base changes of summands of orthonormalizable finite-level Banach sheaves. One compact open subgroup preserves the chart and acts compatibly on every stage.

items.name: Global analytic base change
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. Tensoring VB^0(F) from O^sm to O_Sh gives π_HT^*F for such nilradical-annihilated sheaves.

items.name: Locally analytic functions as descended Cla
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. VB^0(Cla) is O_Sh^la with its prescribed commuting actions.

items.name: Exact Bruhat coefficient descent
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. VB^0 is exact on compatible (g,B)-equivariant nilradical-annihilated LB sheaves on the dagger Bruhat cell C_w†.

items.name: Uniform dagger Banach presentations
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. Over each quasi-compact chart above C_w choose cofinal strict neighborhoods, finite-level Banach summands and a SINGLE compact B-subgroup preserving all neighborhoods and actions. Their colimit is the restricted VB^0(F).

items.name: Dagger analytic base change
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. On the dagger-cell preimage, VB^0(F)⊗_{O^sm}O equals π_HT^*F with the given B-action.

items.name: Restriction compatibility of VB
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. Global-to-Bruhat restriction commutes with VB^0, including the group-linearization and the finite-level presentations.

items.name: Horizontal arithmetic Sen operator
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. For a coefficient sheaf descended from the rational flag variety or rational dagger cell, Θ_hor(μ) on VB^0(F) is its arithmetic Sen operator.

items.name: Smooth coefficients from matching actions
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. If the Lie action equals the derivative of the geometric group action, its descended VB^0 is smooth for the level group.

items.name: Character-smooth coefficients
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. If the two infinitesimal actions differ by the stated character λ, VB^0 is λ-smooth; retain the sign fixed by the difference action and the source character twist.

items.name: Sen descent on completed analytic cohomology
items.statement: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement. Locally analytic completed cohomology after C_p extension has arithmetic Sen descent, and its Sen action agrees with the horizontal μ action supplied by VB.

items.name: Smoothness of HCS coefficients
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)) is λ-smooth for the B-action, by the compatible derivative calculation.

items.name: Finite Levi module comparison
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). For a finite-dimensional simple Levi module, the descended HCS sheaf is the corresponding classical smooth automorphic bundle, with its specified algebraic B-character twist.

items.name: Big overconvergent automorphic bundle
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). For algebraic weight κ, define ω_w^{†,κ}=VB^0(HCS_{w,−w⁻¹w₀,Mκ}(M(m_w)_{−w⁻¹w₀,Mκ})), using the Levi Verma module and its contravariant coefficient functor.

items.name: Classical-to-big coefficient inclusion
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). For M-dominant κ, dual completion of the Verma-to-simple quotient yields an injection of the classical bundle tensored with the negative source B-character into ω_w^{†,κ}.

items.name: Bruhat-support cohomology
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). For the locally closed inclusion j_w:π_HT⁻¹(C_w)→Sh^tor, define RΓ_w(F)=RΓ(Sh^tor,j_{w,!}F), where ! is extension by zero for abelian/solid sheaves and is not a coherent-sheaf functor.

items.name: Extending the action on support cohomology
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). The B-positive action obtained from the support correspondences upgrades to the stipulated B-action on the supported complex, using the λ-smooth coefficient action.

items.name: Bruhat Cousin spectral sequence
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). The finite Bruhat filtration gives E₁ terms given by the direct sums of supported cohomology in each length and converges to global cohomology, with the boundary differential induced by localization triangles.

items.name: Root-coordinate support neighborhoods
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). Define Z_n,U_n around the Bruhat support by inequalities on root coordinates and Z_{n,m},U_{n,m} by additional transverse bounds, with n,m chosen in the cofinal systems of §4.6.28.

items.name: Closed-support colimit formula
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). For the root-coordinate exhaustion F_n⊂V_n, RΓ_w(F) is the filtered colimit of RΓ_{F_n}(V_n,F), compatibly with coefficient and level changes.

items.name: Transverse-neighborhood comparison
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). The same supported cohomology is obtained after the transverse neighborhood limit in m, using the localization triangles and cofinality of the chosen support systems.

items.name: Stein neighborhoods for Bruhat supports
items.statement: Use Bruhat coordinates u_α on U_w, with A=Φ⁺∩w⁻¹Φ^{−,M}, B=Φ⁻∩w⁻¹Φ^{−,M} and fixed n₀≥0. Set X_{n,ε}={|u_α|≤|p|^{n₀−n+ε} for α∈A}; X_n=⋃_{ε∈Q>0}X_{n,ε}. Add |u_α|≤|p|^{m+ε} for α∈B to define X_{n,m,ε}, and take its union X_{n,m}. Define T_{n,m,r,η} by some α∈B satisfying |u_α|≥|p|^{r−η}, and T_{n,m,r}=⋃_{η∈Q>0}T_{n,m,r,η}. Pull back X_n,X_{n,m},T_{n,m,r} by π_HT to Y_n,Y_{n,m},W_{n,m,r}; the printed reversed subscripts T_{m,n,r} in the last pullback must be T_{n,m,r}. These give increasing relatively compact Stein X_n, decreasing X_{n,m}, ⋂_mX_{n,m}=X_n and ⋃_rT_{n,m,r}=X_{n,m}∖X_n.

items.name: Compact-support exhaustion comparison
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). For nested Y_n⊂F_n⊂Y_{n+1}, the comparison maps are RΓ_c(Y_n)→RΓ_{F_n}→RΓ_c(Y_{n+1}); their colimits identify the two support constructions. The printed arrow order needs reversal.

items.name: Compact localization for transverse complements
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). Compact-support localization triangles for the Stein neighborhoods and their annular complements compute the Bruhat complex and remain compatible in the cofinal indices.

items.name: Higher Coleman functor
items.statement: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)). Define HC_{w,λ}(M)=RΓ_w(VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M))); the cusp functor inserts I^sm after VB^0. Both are contravariant derived functors on the indicated parabolic category O.

items.name: Solid Tate acyclicity
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. If X is affinoid and F is coherent, RΓ(X,F) is concentrated in degree0.

items.name: Finite affinoid Čech comparison
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. If X is finite type and F coherent, a finite affinoid cover computes RΓ(X,F) by its Čech complex; separatedness makes its intersections affinoid.
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Solid quasi-Stein acyclicity
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. If X is quasi-Stein and F coherent, RΓ(X,F)=Γ(X,F)[0]. Use a countable affinoid exhaustion with dense restriction maps and the topological Mittag–Leffler theorem; the printed additional word affinoid is unnecessary.

items.name: Banach and Smith coefficients on quasi-Stein spaces
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. If X is finite type, F coherent and V a Banach or Smith E-space, RΓ(X,F⊗_E V)≅RΓ(X,F)⊗_E V. Local freeness and a quasi-Stein hypothesis are not needed here.

items.name: Finite quasi-Stein-cover coefficients
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. For coherent F and Banach or Smith E-space V, if X has a finite quasi-Stein cover then RΓ(X,F⊗_E V)≅RΓ(X,F)⊗_E V. If X itself is quasi-Stein this equals Γ(X,F)⊗_E V in degree0.

items.name: Compactly supported analytic cohomology
items.statement: Let E be a complete nonarchimedean coefficient field of characteristic zero. Use rigid/adic analytic spaces over E with the specified affinoid, quasi-Stein or smooth Stein hypotheses; all tensor products and duals in the coefficient refinements are solid/continuous as specified. RΓ_c(X,F) is the filtered colimit of RΓ_Z(X,F) over closed supports Z proper over the ground analytic point, using the ambient compactifications when required.

items.name: Extension by zero and compact supports
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. Let X be quasi-compact, j:U→X open, and U=⋃_n U_n an increasing quasi-compact open exhaustion with U_n relatively compact in U_{n+1}. For any solid abelian sheaf F on U, RΓ(X,j!F)≅RΓ_c(U,F)≅colim_Z RΓ_Z(U,F), where Z is closed in X and contained in U. There are cofinal closed Z_n with U_n⊂Z_n⊂U_{n+1} and quasi-compact complements in X.

items.name: Chiarellotto Stein concentration
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. If X is smooth Stein of pure dimension d and F locally free coherent, RΓ_c(X,F) is concentrated in degree d.

items.name: Stein coherent Serre duality
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. For smooth Stein X of pure dimension d and locally free coherent F, H_c^d(X,F) is an LB space of compact type and equals Hom_E(Γ(X,Hom_{O_X}(F,Ω_X^d)),E), with continuous/solid Hom.

items.name: Stein duality with Banach–Smith coefficients
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite, and work with separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(E,O_E); cohomology and tensor products are in solid E-modules. For smooth Stein X of pure dimension d, locally free coherent F, and a Smith E-space V, RΓ_c(X,F⊗V)≅RΓ_c(X,F)⊗V is concentrated in degree d, and H_c^d(X,F⊗V)≅Hom_E(Γ(X,Hom(F,Ω_X^d)⊗V∨),E). Smoothness is inherited from the preceding duality theorem; this is not an assertion for singular Stein spaces.

items.name: Locally trivial formal Banach sheaf
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be the admissible formal O_E-model in §4.6.36, with generic fibre X; p-adic completeness refers to the displayed sheaf inverse limit, not merely completeness of individual stalks. A flat O_E-module sheaf 𝔉 on 𝔛 is such a sheaf if 𝔉=lim_n𝔉/pⁿ and locally each reduction is O_{𝔛_n} tensored over O_E/pⁿ with a direct sum of copies of O_E/pⁿ, with the standard compatible reduction maps.

items.name: Very small formal Banach sheaf
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be the admissible formal O_E-model in §4.6.36, with generic fibre X; p-adic completeness refers to the displayed sheaf inverse limit, not merely completeness of individual stalks. A flat complete 𝔉 is very small when 𝔉/p=G₁⊗_{O_E}(⊕_I O_E/p) for a coherent G₁ and a set I, with no assertion that G₁ is locally free.
api: base change of the direct-sum factor

items.name: Locally trivial formal Smith sheaf
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be the admissible formal O_E-model in §4.6.36, with generic fibre X; p-adic completeness refers to the displayed sheaf inverse limit, not merely completeness of individual stalks. Replace the direct sums in the formal Banach definition by products (O_E/pⁿ)^I, tensoring over O_E/pⁿ and retaining flatness, completeness and compatible trivializations.
api: continuous dual of a Banach model

items.name: Very small formal Smith sheaf
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be the admissible formal O_E-model in §4.6.36, with generic fibre X; p-adic completeness refers to the displayed sheaf inverse limit, not merely completeness of individual stalks. A flat complete 𝔉 is very small Smith if its mod-p reduction is G₁⊗_{O_E/p}(O_E/p)^I for coherent G₁; the source tensor over E is ill-typed and must be corrected.

items.name: Rational acyclicity of very small models
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be the admissible formal O_E-model in §4.6.36, with generic fibre X; p-adic completeness refers to the displayed sheaf inverse limit, not merely completeness of individual stalks. If 𝔛 admits an ample line bundle, X is affinoid and 𝔉 is very small formal Banach or Smith, then H^i(𝔛,𝔉)⊗_{O_E}E=0 for i>0.

items.name: Local Banach models for HCS coefficients
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. Near w choose decreasing quasi-compact affinoid flag neighborhoods with intersection in C_w, tower preimages descending at shrinking finite levels, and Banach sheaves whose pullback colimit is the coefficient sheaf. They arise from locally trivial very small formal Banach models.

items.name: Local Smith models for dual HCS coefficients
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. The dual coefficient construction admits the corresponding local presentation by generic fibres of locally trivial very small formal Smith sheaves, with compatible neighborhood and finite-level data.

items.name: Seed cusp acyclicity
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. On an affinoid flag neighborhood stabilized at sufficiently small finite level, the Banach coefficient tensored with the boundary ideal has no positive cohomology; use the toroidal-to-minimal boundary vanishing and very small models.

items.name: Seed compact-support concentration
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. On a stabilized Stein flag neighborhood, the corresponding Smith coefficient on its finite-level tower preimage has compact-support cohomology only in degree d.

items.name: Cuspidal higher Coleman amplitude
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. HC_{cusp,w,λ}(M) has cohomology only in degrees 0 through ℓ(w).

items.name: Noncuspidal higher Coleman amplitude
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. HC_{w,λ}(M) has cohomology only in degrees ℓ(w) through d. The complement-cover proof uses d−ℓ(w) transverse pieces.

items.name: Derived finite-slope localization
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. For the positive-torus monoid representation, finite slope is derived analytic localization to its character space Z=W×(G_m^an)^r; use the pullback/pushforward localization functors, not only algebraic inversion of one Hecke operator.

items.name: Torus slope bound
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. With v(p)=1, a torus eigencharacter has slope given by its valuation character; bounds use the dominance order defined by T⁺. Define ≤,=,≥ truncations and recover finite slope through the compatible bounds.

items.name: Compact-operator bounded slopes
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. For a compact operator on the indicated Banach presentation, each finite-slope bound has finite-dimensional generalized eigenspaces and the source direct-summand decomposition.

items.name: Positive Hecke action on unipotent invariants
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. For compact open K_U⊂U(Q_p), let t∈T⁺ act on M^{K_U} by t followed by trace from tK_Ut⁻¹ to K_U, with the prescribed index normalization.

items.name: Positive-torus monoid law
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. The normalized operators define a T⁺ action on K_U-invariants.

items.name: Trace between unipotent levels
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. For K'_U⊂K_U the trace gives a natural Hecke-compatible map of invariant functors.

items.name: Finite-slope level independence
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. The preceding trace becomes an isomorphism on finite-slope parts, using a strictly contracting torus element.

items.name: Finite-slope higher Coleman functor
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. Define HC^{fs}_{w,λ}(M) by taking compact-unipotent invariants and analytic finite-slope localization; the trace isomorphism makes this independent of K_U. Define the cusp variant identically.

items.name: Classical cuspidal BP comparison
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. For an M-dominant algebraic κ, the finite-slope cusp HC of L(m_w)_{−w⁻¹w₀,Mκ} with λ=0 identifies after Q_p-bar extension with the sum of BP21 coherent complexes RΓ_w(K^p,κ,χ,cusp)^{+,fs} over smooth T(Z_p)-characters χ.

items.name: Classical noncuspidal BP comparison
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. Under the same hypotheses the noncuspidal HC identifies with the corresponding sum of BP21 noncuspidal coherent complexes.

items.name: Verma cuspidal BP comparison
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. For dν=−w⁻¹w₀,M(κ+ρ)−ρ, the finite-slope HC of the Levi Verma of highest weight −w⁻¹w₀,Mκ identifies with the sum of big BP21 cusp complexes over locally analytic ν' with derivative dν.

items.name: Verma noncuspidal BP comparison
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. For dν=−w⁻¹w₀,M(κ+ρ)−ρ, the finite-slope HC of the Levi Verma of highest weight −w⁻¹w₀,Mκ identifies with the sum of big BP21 noncuspidal complexes over locally analytic ν' with derivative dν. The identification preserves the T(Q_p) action, with the direct sum on the right the T(Z_p)-isotypic decomposition.

items.name: Finite-slope cusp amplitude
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. HC^{fs}_{cusp,w,λ}(M) is concentrated in 0,…,ℓ(w); the proof uses the compact Banach presentations and bounded-slope exactness.

items.name: Finite-slope noncusp amplitude
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. HC^{fs}_{w,λ}(M) is concentrated in ℓ(w),…,d under the same finite-slope construction.

items.name: Sharp highest-weight slope bound
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. If Sh is proper or is a Siegel Shimura variety, and M is generated by a highest-weight vector ν, slopes in both HC^{fs}_{w,λ}(M) and its cusp variant are at least λ−ν+w⁻¹w₀,Mρ+ρ.

items.name: General Hodge-type slope bound
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor. Without properness or the Siegel assumption only the weaker bound λ−ν is supplied by the argument; the sharper general bound is recorded as a conjectural extension, not a theorem.

items.name: Completed cohomology with category-O coefficients
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. CC_λ(M)=RHom_g(M,RΓ(Sh^tor,E)^la) with the λ-adjusted B-action; its cusp analogue uses RΓ_c. The M argument is contravariant and finite-slope truncations use the induced positive Hecke action.

items.name: Derived p-adic Eichler–Shimura comparison
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. For every such M, CC_λ(M)⊗C_p≅RΓ(Sh^tor,VB_red(Loc(M))).

items.name: Cuspidal derived comparison
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. The cusp CC comparison inserts I^sm in the coefficient complex after VB_red.

items.name: Sen compatibility of the derived comparison
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. The horizontal action of μ on Loc(M) induces the arithmetic Sen operator on the completed-cohomology side.

items.name: Reduced coefficients commute with cohomology
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. If λ is non-Liouville, H^i(VB_red(Loc(M)))=VB^0(H^i(Loc(M))). This imports the completed nilradical-homology comparison and its recorded proof gate.

items.name: Higher Coleman spectral sequence
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. For non-Liouville λ, E₁^{a,b}=⊕_{ℓ(w)=a}H^{a+b}(HC_{w,λ}(E⊗^L_{u_{P_w}}M)) converges to H^{a+b}(CC_λ(M))⊗C_p.

items.name: Cuspidal higher Coleman spectral sequence
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. For non-Liouville λ the same spectral sequence holds with cusp HC and cusp CC.

items.name: Sen action on the spectral sequence
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. On each w term, wμ∈Z(m_w) acting on nilradical homology induces the arithmetic Sen action on the abutment.

items.name: Antidominant proper concentration
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. If λ is non-Liouville and antidominant in the sense of §2.3, and Sh is proper, CC_λ(M(g)_λ) is concentrated in degree d.

items.name: Antidominant proper filtration
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. If λ is non-Liouville and antidominant and the Shimura variety is proper, H^d has a decreasing filtration with Gr^a=⊕_{ℓ(w)=a}H^a(HC_{w,λ}(M(m_w)_{λ+w⁻¹w₀,Mρ+ρ})), after C_p extension. The filtration has Fil⁰=H^d and Fil^{d+1}=0.

items.name: Nonnegative Verma slopes
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. For non-Liouville λ and proper or Siegel Sh, both cusp and usual CC^{fs}_λ(M(g)_λ) have slopes at least zero.

items.name: Ordinary Eichler–Shimura sequence
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. For non-Liouville λ and a proper or Siegel Shimura variety, the ordinary E₁^{a,b} term is ⊕_{ℓ(w)=a}H^{2a+b−d}(HC^{=0}_{w,λ}(M(m_w)_{λ+w⁻¹w₀,Mρ+ρ})); it converges to ordinary CC^{a+b}⊗C_p, also in the cusp case.

items.name: Proper ordinary concentration
items.statement: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1. For proper Sh and non-Liouville λ, ordinary CC_λ(M(g)_λ) is concentrated in degree d, without an antidominance hypothesis.

items.name: Classical Siegel Hodge–Tate decomposition
items.statement: Specialize to GSp4 and d=3, with the paper Borel and four representatives w_j of length j. For algebraic G-dominant κ=(k₁,k₂;w), 0≥k₁≥k₂ and the parity condition holds; write V_κ for its algebraic representation. Classical coherent bundles here have the untwisted normalization of §4.8. H^i(Sh,V_κ∨)⊗C_p=⊕_{j=0}³H^{i−j}(Sh,ω^{κ_j})(−a_j), where κ_j are (k₁,k₂;−w),(2−k₁,k₂;−w),(3−k₂,k₁+1;−w),(3−k₂,3−k₁;−w), and 2a_j are k₁+k₂+w,2−k₁+k₂+w,4−k₂+k₁+w,6−k₁−k₂+w.

items.name: Cuspidal classical Hodge–Tate decomposition
items.statement: Specialize to GSp4 and d=3, with the paper Borel and four representatives w_j of length j. For algebraic G-dominant κ=(k₁,k₂;w), 0≥k₁≥k₂ and the parity condition holds; write V_κ for its algebraic representation. Classical coherent bundles here have the untwisted normalization of §4.8. The same decomposition holds with compact-support étale cohomology and coherent coefficients tensored with the boundary ideal.

items.name: Algebraic coefficient comparison with completed cohomology
items.statement: Specialize to GSp4 and d=3, with the paper Borel and four representatives w_j of length j. For algebraic G-dominant κ=(k₁,k₂;w), 0≥k₁≥k₂ and the parity condition holds; write V_κ for its algebraic representation. Classical coherent bundles here have the untwisted normalization of §4.8. For a finite algebraic coefficient, derived Lie-Hom into locally analytic completed cohomology recovers the filtered colimit of its finite-level étale cohomology, with the stated group and Galois actions.

items.name: Classical comparison on completed coefficients
items.statement: Specialize to GSp4 and d=3, with the paper Borel and four representatives w_j of length j. For algebraic G-dominant κ=(k₁,k₂;w), 0≥k₁≥k₂ and the parity condition holds; write V_κ for its algebraic representation. Classical coherent bundles here have the untwisted normalization of §4.8. The preceding algebraic-coefficient comparison transports the four-term classical Hodge–Tate decomposition to CC, including the cusp version and its Tate weights.

items.name: Siegel ordinary spectral sequence
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. The ordinary Eichler–Shimura sequence has these four big-coefficient Bruhat terms, with degree placement E₁^{a,b}=H^{2a+b−3}_{w_a}; use the cusp version for compact support.

items.name: Big degree-zero extremal support
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. For every big weight κ, H⁰_w(ω_w^{†,κ})^{fs} and its cusp version vanish unless w=w₀ of length zero.

items.name: Big degree-three extremal support
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. For every κ, H³_w(ω_w^{†,κ})^{fs} and its cusp version vanish unless w=w₃.

items.name: Classical degree-zero extremal support
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. For M-dominant κ, ordinary or finite-slope H⁰_w of the classical bundle, with or without boundary ideal, vanishes unless w has length zero.

items.name: Classical degree-three extremal support
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. For M-dominant κ the corresponding H³_w vanishes unless w=w₃.

items.name: Cuspidal ordinary completed amplitude
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Before residual localization the ordinary cusp Verma completed complex is supported in degrees1,…,3.

items.name: Cuspidal ordinary filtration before localization
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Its degree3 graded pieces are coker(H¹_{w₂}(−D)→H³_{w₃}(−D)), H²_{w₂}(−D), H¹_{w₁}(−D), H⁰_{w₀}(−D); degree2 has H²_{w₃}(−D) and the kernel of that map; degree1 is H¹_{w₃}(−D).

items.name: Noncuspidal ordinary completed amplitude
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Before localization the noncuspidal ordinary Verma complex is supported in degrees3,…,5.

items.name: Noncuspidal ordinary filtration before localization
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Degree3 has H³_{w₃},H²_{w₂},H¹_{w₁},ker(H⁰_{w₀}→H²_{w₁}); degree4 has that map's cokernel and H¹_{w₀}; degree5 has H²_{w₀}.

items.name: Non-Eisenstein boundary vanishing
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. At the irreducible residual maximal ideal, the map from cusp to ordinary completed cohomology is an isomorphism. This uses the source-qualified boundary theorem of Newton–Thorne, not genericity alone.

items.name: Bruhat coefficient boundary vanishing
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. At the same residual ideal, cusp-to-noncusp ordinary big cohomology is an isomorphism on every Bruhat piece.

items.name: Ordinary degree-zero boundary is Eisenstein
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. The degree-zero boundary of the higher-Hida complex vanishes at this residual ideal, using normalization of the ordinary Igusa boundary and the GL2/GSp4 Hecke comparison.

items.name: Localized ordinary middle-degree concentration
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. At the irreducible residual ideal, the ordinary Verma/Borel completed complex is concentrated in degree3.

items.name: Four-piece ordinary filtration
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Its degree3 cohomology after C_p extension has Gr^j=H^j_{w_j}, j=0,…,3, with the specified big coefficient and B-character twist.

items.name: Sen eigenvalues on ordinary pieces
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. On Gr^3,Gr^2,Gr^1,Gr^0 respectively, the Sen eigenvalues are (−λ₁−λ₂−w)/2,(−2+λ₁−λ₂−w)/2,(−4+λ₂−λ₁−w)/2,(−6+λ₁+λ₂−w)/2.

items.name: Classical singular-weight support
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. Ordinary classical ω^{(1,1;−w)} cohomology is supported on the union of the length2 and length3 Bruhat strata.

items.name: Classical singular Cousin complex
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. That cohomology is represented by H²_{w₂}(ω^{(1,1;−w)})→H³_{w₃}(ω^{(1,1;−w)}) in degrees2 and3, with differential the geometric Cousin boundary.

items.name: Classical-to-big singular comparison
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. The classical-to-big maps on these two supported ordinary terms are isomorphisms, by the rank-one BGG sequence and the slope exclusion of its kernel.

items.name: Generalized Sen eigenspace extension
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. The generalized a eigenspace V[(Θ−a)²] is an extension of Gr² by Gr³, with Θ−a inducing a map Gr²→Gr³; similarly the generalized b eigenspace uses Gr⁰ and Gr¹.

items.name: Sen operator and Cousin boundary
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. Under the classical/big identifications, the map Gr²→Gr³ induced by Θ−a is a NONZERO scalar multiple of the classical Cousin differential. Its source proof imports the unresolved constrained-fibre comparison3.6.15 through3.6.9.

items.name: Minuscule GSp4 semisimplicity criterion
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite and enlarge coefficients as needed. Continuous G_Q-representations are unramified outside finitely many primes. Polynomial-annihilation conditions below are required on a density-one set of unramified Frobenius classes, not merely equality of traces. If ρ:G_Q→GSp4(E-bar) has Zariski closure containing Sp4 and every characteristic polynomial of ρ(Frob_ℓ) annihilates s(Frob_ℓ), then the finite-dimensional representation s is a direct sum of copies of ρ.

items.name: Induced symplectic semisimplicity criterion
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite and enlarge coefficients as needed. Continuous G_Q-representations are unramified outside finitely many primes. Polynomial-annihilation conditions below are required on a density-one set of unramified Frobenius classes, not merely equality of traces. The same conclusion holds if ρ is irreducible, restricts to ϱ⊕ϱ^c over an index-two subgroup G_E, and its Zariski closure contains SL2×SL2. The mixed-extension proof uses reciprocal eigenvalues λ,λ⁻¹ on the determinant−1 component of O4.

items.name: Galois representation of an ordinary overconvergent form
items.statement: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}. There is a continuous semisimple ρ_f:G_Q→GSp4(Q_p-bar), unramified outside the prescribed S, whose Frobenius polynomial away from S is P_ℓ modulo m_f.

items.name: Ordinary local characters of the interpolated representation
items.statement: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}. The local representation is Borel-valued with diagonal characters χ₄⁻¹z^{−1−w/2},χ₃⁻¹z^{−1−w/2},χ₂⁻¹z^{−2−w/2},χ₁⁻¹z^{−2−w/2} under local reciprocity, including evaluation at p. Remove the duplicated inverses in the printed last two entries.

items.name: Isotypic completed eigenspace
items.statement: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}. Assume ρ̄_f irreducible and either Sp4 Zariski image or the induced SL2×SL2 hypothesis of4.11.2. Then V[m_f]≅ρ_f⊗W with W finite-dimensional and nonzero, using finite-slope control and Frobenius polynomial annihilation.

items.name: Balanced-multiplicity classicality
items.statement: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}. Assume those image hypotheses, ρ_f locally de Rham, ρ̄_f irreducible, and an integer n with dim_Cp Gr^i(V⊗C_p)[m_f]=n for every i=0,…,3 and dim_Qpbar V[m_f]=4n. Then f is classical. These are eigenspace dimensions; exactness of the eigenspace functor is not an assumption one may omit or infer without the balance.

items.name: Polarized general linear group
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. Define the disconnected group scheme G_n with the displayed semidirect multiplication, identity component and multiplier, including its congruence kernel over a local coefficient ring.

items.name: Polarized representation
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. An absolutely irreducible ρ:G_F→GL_n(k) is polarized by μ:G_F⁺→k× if it has a perfect pairing with ⟨ρ(g)x,ρ(cgc)y⟩=μ(g)⟨x,y⟩ and ⟨x,y⟩=−μ(c)⟨y,x⟩.
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Extension of a polarized representation
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. Such a polarized pair extends to r:G_F⁺→G_n(k) with preimage of the identity component G_F and multiplier μ; the extension is unique up to G_n⁰-conjugacy in the stated absolutely irreducible setting.

items.name: Symplectic group with sign
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. On GSp_{2m}×{±1} define the multiplier to be the symplectic multiplier on the first factor, ignoring the sign factor.

items.name: Symplectic-to-unitary group embedding
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. For standard J, the source explicit map sends (g,+1) to (g,νg) and (g,−1) to (g,νg)(J⁻¹,−1)j; it embeds GSp_{2m}×{±1} into G_{2m} preserving the specified multiplier.

items.name: CM polarization of a symplectic representation
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. Combine a symplectic G_F⁺ representation with the CM quotient sign and the preceding embedding to obtain a polarized G_{2m} representation with unchanged multiplier and identity-component preimage G_F.

items.name: Strong residual oddness
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. In characteristic2 the polarized pair is strongly residually odd at a real place v if r(c_v) is GL_n(k)-conjugate to (I,1)j. This is stronger than the multiplier condition μ(c_v)=1.

items.name: Strong oddness through symplectic involutions
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. For a symplectic involution A over perfect k of characteristic2, its polarized image is strongly odd precisely when the associated nonsingular symmetric form AJ is nonalternating; classify the congruence forms before applying this criterion.

items.name: Rank classification of strong involutions
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. With r=rank(A−1), odd r is strongly odd; for positive even r the strong class is the one with nonalternating residual symmetric form. The other class and the identity are not strong.

items.name: Strong involutions under Sp4(F2)=S6
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. In the paper S6 identification, transpositions and double transpositions are strongly odd, whereas triple transpositions are not.

items.name: Trace detection and semisimple span
items.statement: Let V=k^n for a subfield k⊂F₂-bar and finite H⊂GL(V), with ad=End_k(V) carrying conjugation and ad⁰=ker(trace). All group-cohomology coefficients and trace projectors below use this characteristic2 representation. The semisimple elements span End(V) exactly when every simple submodule W of ad (equivalently the source ad⁰ test) has some eigenprojector e_{σ,α} for semisimple σ with nonzero trace pairing on W.

items.name: Weak adequacy
items.statement: Let V=k^n for a subfield k⊂F₂-bar and finite H⊂GL(V), with ad=End_k(V) carrying conjugation and ad⁰=ker(trace). All group-cohomology coefficients and trace projectors below use this characteristic2 representation. H is weakly adequate if its semisimple elements span End_k(V); equivalently use the preceding trace-detection criterion. In particular this implies absolute irreducibility.

items.name: Near adequacy
items.statement: Let V=k^n for a subfield k⊂F₂-bar and finite H⊂GL(V), with ad=End_k(V) carrying conjugation and ad⁰=ker(trace). All group-cohomology coefficients and trace projectors below use this characteristic2 representation. H is nearly adequate if it is weakly adequate, H¹(H,k)=0 and H¹(H,ad)=0. For a representation, apply this predicate to its finite image.

items.name: Polarized local deformation problem
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. A local problem is a subfunctor of fixed-multiplier framed lifts over CNL_{Λ_v}, stable under the congruence kernel of G_n and satisfying the source deformation-condition axioms.

items.name: Polarized global deformation problem
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. The tuple of F,r̄,O,χ,S,Λ_v and local conditions defines global lifts modulo strict congruence G_n-conjugacy; retain the multiplier and identity-component preimage in families.
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Representing and framed global rings
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Construct R_S and its T-framed version for nonempty T containing all nontrivial coefficient places; framing is formally smooth of relative dimension (n²+1)#T−1 over the unframed ring.

items.name: Extra polarized tangent direction
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Let μ_v=ker(H¹(G_{F_v⁺},ad)→H¹(G_{F_v⁺},Lie G_n)); it is the image of the connecting map from k for 0→ad→Lie G_n→k→0.

items.name: Relative polarized deformation complex
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Form the mapping-fibre complex imposing local tangent conditions outside T and framing conditions on T; for degrees≥3 its local summands use C^{i−1}(F_v⁺,ad), correcting the cited Thorne typo.

items.name: Dyadic polarized dual Selmer group
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Define H¹_{S⊥,T} as the kernel of global H¹(ad(1)) to local quotients by μ_v⊥ at T and L_v⊥ outside T, under local Tate trace duality.

items.name: Polarized deformation presentation
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. For T nonempty the relative complex has the tangent/obstruction groups in degrees1,2, h²=h¹_{S⊥,T}, and a local-ring power-series presentation with the resulting tangent and relation bounds.

items.name: Dyadic Taylor–Wiles block condition
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. At a split unramified auxiliary place choose an eigenvalue α of semisimple residual Frobenius and its generalized α-block A; lifts have the complementary block unramified and inertia scalar on A via the universal character of the2-primary residue units.

items.name: Dyadic Taylor–Wiles datum
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. A level-N datum is a finite set Q of such split places with q_v≡1 mod2^N, choices α_v and local block conditions; Δ_Q is the product of2-primary residue-unit groups.

items.name: Unavoidable dyadic dual-Selmer class
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. The first real cyclotomic quadratic extension outside F⁺ supplies a nonzero scalar dual-Selmer class, and every allowed Taylor–Wiles datum leaves it unremoved. Choose K_m⁺ not contained in F⁺ with K_{m−1}⁺ contained in F⁺; the printed reverse containment is false.

items.name: Trace detection of a restricted cocycle
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Under near adequacy, a nonzero relevant class restricted to the cyclotomic field remains nonzero after restriction to the field cut out by ad r̄; semisimple eigenprojector detection then produces the needed Chebotarev value.

items.name: Near-adequate auxiliary primes
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Assume additionally F=F⁺(i), unrestricted real conditions with χ(c_v)=−1, near adequacy of ρ̄(G_F), and strong oddness at some real place if n is even. Set T=S\S_∞, q=h¹_{S⊥,T}−1 and g=q+#T−1−[F⁺:Q]n(n−1)/2. For every N there are infinitely many level-N data with #Q=q and R_loc[[X₁,…,X_g]] surjecting onto R^T_{S_Q}.

items.name: Uniform potentially unipotent ramification
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. At a place away from2 there is a single finite local extension on which every lift of the fixed residual representation has unipotent inertia, using finiteness of deformation-ring components and constancy of inertial types.

items.name: Uniformly unramified regular residual lifts
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. If q_v≡1 mod2 and residual Frobenius is unramified regular semisimple, every lift is a sum of characters; a uniform finite local extension makes all lifts unramified.

items.name: Prescribed inertial characteristic polynomial
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. For finite-order characters χ_{v,j} congruent to1, impose det(X−ρ(σ))=∏_j(X−χ_{v,j}(Art_v(σ))⁻¹) for σ in inertia; define the source reduced flat local ring with this condition.

items.name: Unipotent-type local components
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. For trivial residual representation and all χ_{v,j}=1 in the source q_v≡1 mod2 setting, each component has dimension n²+1, every special-fibre minimal prime lifts to a unique generic minimal prime, and the generic points have characteristic zero.

items.name: Distinct-inertia local irreducibility
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. For pairwise distinct χ_{v,j} in that setting the type deformation ring is irreducible of dimension n²+1.

items.name: Ordinary GLn local ring
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. There is a reduced2-torsion-free ordinary local ring R_v△ over Λ_{GL_n,v}, represented by the appropriate scheme image of the stable full-flag incidence space.

items.name: Ordinary GLn integral points
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. For every finite E'/E and weight-algebra map to O_E', a framed lift factors through R_v△ exactly when it is upper triangular with ordered inertia characters equal to the corresponding universal character components.

items.name: Large-degree ordinary components
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. If the residual representation is trivial and [F_v⁺:Q₂]>n(n−1)/2+1, then for each minimal prime Q of Λ_{GL_n,v}, R_v△/Q is geometrically irreducible of dimension [F_v⁺:Q₂]n(n+1)/2+n²+1 and its mod-uniformizer fibre is generically reduced.

items.name: Flatness of the flag scheme image
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. Under that local degree hypothesis the ordinary flag incidence scheme image is already flat, so taking an additional flat closure does not alter the GLn ring used here.

items.name: Ordinary algebraic weight
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. A representation is ordinary of weight λ if it has a full stable flag with rank-one quotients whose characters on sufficiently small units α are ∏_ττ(α)^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1)} for the ith quotient.

items.name: Definite unitary integral model
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. Construct this unitary group and its split finite-place integral identifications, using the parity condition and local invariants.

items.name: Definite unitary algebraic forms
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. S_λ(U,O) consists of functions on G(F⁺)\G(A_F⁺^∞) transforming under U by the algebraic coefficient M_λ, tensor-indexed by embeddings of the2-adic fields, with any prescribed Iwahori character factors.

items.name: Sufficiently small unitary level
items.statement: For the definite unitary group G/F⁺ of §5.7, a compact open U⊂G(A_F⁺^∞) is sufficiently small if, for some finite place v, its projection to G(F⁺_v) has no nonidentity finite-order element. This makes every arithmetic double-quotient stabilizer trivial.

items.name: Ordinary unitary Hecke algebra
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4.
