For unramified mod3 type4C or12C, no residual Frobenius root ratio is2, so any lift is unramified by the adjoint obstruction calculation. Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich then forces good reduction, ruling out semistable distinguished realizations of these types.

items.name: Three elementary local-two products
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point. Take a Tate elliptic X/Q₂ with parameter a sixth power, and ordinary Y with full rational2-torsion and Q_Y=X²+X+2; let primes denote unramified quadratic twists. The products X×Y,Y×Y',X×X' have projective3-types8A,4D,2D, trivial mod2 image and distinct ordinary unit roots; only Y×Y' has good reduction.

items.name: Two quartics excluded by local-two image
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point. The ordinary quartics X⁴±3X³+5X²±6X+4 reduce to X²(X²+X+1) mod2 and cannot occur with the required S5(b) local2-image.

items.name: Three-torsion rigidity for the6H isogeny class
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point. Every F2 abelian surface with Q=X⁴−X²+4 has projective3-torsion type6H. The isogeny reduction uses ψ=φ²+1 with ψ∨ψ=6 to remove3-factors from an isogeny to the explicit reference Jacobian.

items.name: Toric reduction in the2C and6G cases
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point. For unramified mod3 projective type2C or6G and mod2 image in S5(b), ADD the hypothesis of bad reduction; then semistability and the irreducible residual quadratic exclude toric rank1, so reduction is purely toric. The printed statement without this extra hypothesis is false; the source good nonordinary curve in9.2.16 is a counterexample.

items.name: Order-four twist realizing2C
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point. Take a Tate X with cubic parameter q in5Q₂×², twist X² by the unramified order-four orthogonal matrix [[0,−1],[1,0]], and descend the product polarization. The result is purely toric ordinary and2-distinguished with mod2 image in S5(b) and unramified mod3 type2C. The3-torsion factor is(1⊕ε̄⁻¹)⊗R, not I⊗R.

items.name: Explicit6G level-three specialization
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point. Start from Y:y²+y=x⁵−x⁴+x³, which has good NONordinary reduction at2 and Q₂=X⁴+2X²+4. Apply the source rational twisted-level-three parametrization and specialization to obtain a bad-reduction curve with the same3-torsion; retain the exact rational parameters as a separate finite algebraic certificate.

items.name: Small6G toric example
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point. For X:y²+(−x²−x−1)y=x⁵−4x⁴+47x³−43x²−2x+8, the source division-polynomial/conductor calculation gives a rational Weierstrass point, purely toric2-distinguished Jacobian, unramified3-torsion and projective type6G. Those conductor/resolvent assertions were not executed in this audit.

items.name: Exclusion of good ordinary2D
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point. Every F2 surface with Q=X⁴+X²+4 has projective3-type6I, by reducing isogenies through the two φ±1 degree-six factors. Thus projective2D has no good ordinary realization with the required2-image.

items.name: Genus-two enumeration over F3
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. Among3⁷ polynomials of degree≤6, the source y²=f(x) enumeration gives1296 smooth genus-two curves and864 ordinary ones. Exactly ten ordinary models have repeated-root Weil quartic; none has an F3-rational Weierstrass point.

items.name: Scalar étale Frobenius for ordinary F3 Jacobians
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. For the ordinary genus-two Jacobians in this enumeration, scalar Frobenius on the étale3-torsion occurs exactly in the nondistinguished square-quartic cases. Do not extend this equivalence to all PPAVs: ordinary products provide counterexamples.

items.name: Ordinary Weil quartics at three
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. There are exactly forty ordinary3-Weil quartics, with the source list verified by exhaustive coefficient/root tests.

items.name: Odd-prime polarized finite-flat lifting
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. For p>2, O a finite p-adic integer ring and G₁/O a principally quasi-polarized finite flat group killed by p of rank p⁴, if a PPAV surface A₀ over the residue field has polarized p-torsion G₁ special fibre, then A₀ lifts to a PPAV A/O with A[p]≅G₁. The printed rank4 must be p⁴; use the truncated BT lifting theorem, Serre–Tate and effectivity.

items.name: Jacobian lift of a smooth genus-two special fibre
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. If A₀ is the Jacobian of a smooth genus-two curve, the polarized deformation obtained above is a Jacobian of a smooth lifted curve, using the genus-two Torelli tangent isomorphism.

items.name: Local-three realization from an ordinary special fibre
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. Given an ordinary PPAV A₀/F3 with A₀[3]^et≅V̄ and mod2 image in S5(b), there is a genus-two X/Q₃ with rational Weierstrass point, Jac(X) good ordinary and residual H¹ representation ρ̄. If A₀ is3-distinguished so is Jac(X). Use uniqueness of the finite-flat model over Z₃ and torsion local constancy.

items.name: Nonscalar local-three seed curves
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. The four source quintic examples and their unramified quadratic twists realize the nonscalar conjugacy classes of V̄ with good ordinary distinguished special fibre and a rational Weierstrass point; certify the class through étale3-torsion, not only the quartic.

items.name: Scalar local-three product seed
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. Use elliptic traces−1 and2 over F3, giving product quartic(X²+X+3)(X²−2X+3), étale3-Frobenius scalar−1 and mod2 permutation order6 in S5(b). For scalar+1 take its unramified quadratic twist, with traces1 and−2. The product has distinct unit roots.

items.name: Ordinary local-three realization
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. Every ordinary ρ̄:G_Q₃→GSp4(F3) of multiplier ε̄⁻¹ with finite-flat dual is realized by H¹ of a good ordinary3-distinguished genus-two Jacobian whose curve has a Q₃-rational Weierstrass point.

items.name: Product fibre can force bad curve reduction
items.statement: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters. In the scalar V̄ case a product PPAV may be necessary as the special fibre; a nearby characteristic-zero Jacobian still has good abelian-surface reduction, while its curve need not have good reduction.

items.name: Weak approximation outside a thin set
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹, ordinary finite-flat dual at3 and unramified restriction at2. Use the smooth rational odd-theta space P(ρ̄), its dense Jacobian locus and local constancy of the finite torsion representations on p-adic neighborhoods. For a SMOOTH rational Q-variety Z, finitely many nonempty local open conditions and a fixed thin subset, there is a rational point satisfying those conditions outside the thin set. Smoothness is the needed added hypothesis; a singular isolated real point gives a counterexample to the printed unrestricted statement.

items.name: Local-two Jacobian equivalence
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹, ordinary finite-flat dual at3 and unramified restriction at2. Use the smooth rational odd-theta space P(ρ̄), its dense Jacobian locus and local constancy of the finite torsion representations on p-adic neighborhoods. Projective Frob₂ not of type4C or12C is equivalent to realization of ρ̄ at2 by a genus-two Jacobian with rational Weierstrass point, semistable ordinary reduction and2-distinction.

items.name: Global2–3 switch
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹, ordinary finite-flat dual at3 and unramified restriction at2. Use the smooth rational odd-theta space P(ρ̄), its dense Jacobian locus and local constancy of the finite torsion representations on p-adic neighborhoods. If those equivalent conditions hold, there is a genus-two X/Q with rational Weierstrass point and B=Jac(X) with residual H¹ mod3 equal to ρ̄, semistable ordinary2-distinguished reduction at2, good ordinary reduction at3, full mod2 image S5(b), double-transposition complex conjugation and End(B_Qbar)=Z.

items.name: Full residual image by rational approximation
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹, ordinary finite-flat dual at3 and unramified restriction at2. Use the smooth rational odd-theta space P(ρ̄), its dense Jacobian locus and local constancy of the finite torsion representations on p-adic neighborhoods. In P(ρ̄), avoid the finite covers corresponding to proper subgroups of S5(b), impose the2- and3-adic open conditions and a real quintic with exactly one real root, and pass to the Jacobian open locus. At2 keep semistable ordinary reduction if the local seed has bad reduction.

items.name: Modularity transfer between ordinary surfaces
items.statement: All abelian-surface Galois representations use H¹. Modularity in the following general-type conclusions means a weight2 cuspidal GSp4 form with cuspidal GL4 transfer, and the corresponding H¹ L-function has the expected analytic continuation and functional equation. Source proof gates, including Arthur transfer, remain recorded in this extraction. Let p>2 and A,B/Q have equal mod-p representations and good ordinary reduction at p; assume A p-distinguished, B arises from an ordinary weight2 cuspidal GSp4 form of level prime to p, the Zariski closure of ρ_{A,p} contains Sp4, and ρ̄_{A,p} is reasonable and tidy with regular elements in its cyclotomic-mod-p image and outside Sp4. Then A is modular, via the common finite-flat ordinary component and7.5.11.

items.name: Fifteen-image abelian-surface modularity
items.statement: All abelian-surface Galois representations use H¹. Modularity in the following general-type conclusions means a weight2 cuspidal GSp4 form with cuspidal GL4 transfer, and the corresponding H¹ L-function has the expected analytic continuation and functional equation. Source proof gates, including Arthur transfer, remain recorded in this extraction. Let A/Q have polarization degree prime to3, End(A_Qbar)=Z and mod3 image one of the fifteen ticked groups of6.4.3. If mod3 is unramified at2 with characteristic polynomial different from(X²+X+2)² and(X²−X+2)², and A has good ordinary reduction at3 with distinct Frobenius roots, then A is modular.

items.name: Good-reduction genus-two modularity
items.statement: All abelian-surface Galois representations use H¹. Modularity in the following general-type conclusions means a weight2 cuspidal GSp4 form with cuspidal GL4 transfer, and the corresponding H¹ L-function has the expected analytic continuation and functional equation. Source proof gates, including Arthur transfer, remain recorded in this extraction. Let X/Q be smooth genus2 with End(Jac(X)_Qbar)=Z and one of the fifteen allowed mod3 images. If X has good ordinary reduction at2 and3 and Jac(X) is3-distinguished, then X is modular.

items.name: Quintic genus-two modularity
items.statement: All abelian-surface Galois representations use H¹. Modularity in the following general-type conclusions means a weight2 cuspidal GSp4 form with cuspidal GL4 transfer, and the corresponding H¹ L-function has the expected analytic continuation and functional equation. Source proof gates, including Arthur transfer, remain recorded in this extraction. For smooth X:y²=f(x) with deg f=5, the same image and endomorphism hypotheses and good ordinary curve reduction at2 and3 imply modularity without an extra3-distinction assumption, by the finite F3 Weierstrass enumeration.

items.name: Bad-at-two abelian-surface modularity
items.statement: All abelian-surface Galois representations use H¹. Modularity in the following general-type conclusions means a weight2 cuspidal GSp4 form with cuspidal GL4 transfer, and the corresponding H¹ L-function has the expected analytic continuation and functional equation. Source proof gates, including Arthur transfer, remain recorded in this extraction. If a prime-to3 polarized A/Q has End(A_Qbar)=Z, one of the fifteen images, unramified mod3 at2, good ordinary distinguished reduction at3 and BAD reduction at2, then A is modular. The bad-reduction hypothesis excludes4C/12C through the toric lattice or the no-root-ratio obstruction, not through a claim that the whole Tate module has finite image.

items.name: Positive coefficient-family proportion
items.statement: The statistical application refers to the paper fixed2024 LMFDB genus-two snapshot and to coefficient-box density in the specified generalized Weierstrass models. It is not a count of the current database and not a theorem about ordering all abelian surfaces by conductor. The local model conditions at2 and3 have product proportion ((768−144)/2¹¹)((864−10)/3⁷)=5551/46656. To deduce generic modularity in this coefficient family also supply density-one full mod3 image, not only End=Z; the latter alone does not imply the required residual image.

items.name: Frozen database application certificate
items.statement: The statistical application refers to the paper fixed2024 LMFDB genus-two snapshot and to coefficient-box density in the specified generalized Weierstrass models. It is not a count of the current database and not a theorem about ordering all abelian surfaces by conductor. The paper2024 dataset has66158 curves; the displayed filters leave11384 good-at2,3 examples for TheoremA and359 further bad-at2 examples, totaling11743. Keep the exact dataset/code revision, row predicates and de-duplication as part of the finite certificate; this is not an intrinsic theorem about a changing database.

items.name: Abelian-surface Galois type
items.statement: Continuous p-adic Galois representations have finite dimension over Q_p-bar and are de Rham at all p-adic places. Potentially abelian means that restriction to some finite Galois extension has abelian image; finite up to twist means a character twist has finite image. Use the FKRS12 classification of the geometric endomorphism algebra with its Galois action, giving34 types over Q. TypeA is the geometrically generic endomorphism case; B[C₂] is the remaining quadratic endomorphism-action case in the source classification.

items.name: Automorphy for thirty-two Galois types
items.statement: Continuous p-adic Galois representations have finite dimension over Q_p-bar and are de Rham at all p-adic places. Potentially abelian means that restriction to some finite Galois extension has abelian image; finite up to twist means a character twist has finite image. If A/Q has Galois type other than A or B[C₂], then A is modular in Definition1.8.25: its H¹ L-function comes from an isobaric GL4 representation, possibly a sum of lower-rank cuspidal pieces.

items.name: Character-orbit induction for potentially abelian representations
items.statement: Continuous p-adic Galois representations have finite dimension over Q_p-bar and are de Rham at all p-adic places. Potentially abelian means that restriction to some finite Galois extension has abelian image; finite up to twist means a character twist has finite image. If irreducible ρ:G_F→GL_n becomes abelian over finite Galois L/F, then ρ restricted to G_L is ⊕_{i=1}^bχ_i^{⊕a}, ab=n, with distinct χ_i in a transitive Galois orbit; for the stabilizer field K_i there is irreducible V_i of dimension a with ρ≅Ind_{G_Ki}^{G_F}V_i and V_i restricted to G_L=χ_i^{⊕a}.

items.name: Nonfinite twists and algebraic Hecke characters
items.statement: Continuous p-adic Galois representations have finite dimension over Q_p-bar and are de Rham at all p-adic places. Potentially abelian means that restriction to some finite Galois extension has abelian image; finite up to twist means a character twist has finite image. If additionally ρ is not finite up to twist, the χ_i are algebraic Hecke characters of nonparallel weight, b>1, and when a=1 each K_i contains an imaginary CM field.

items.name: Two-dimensional potentially abelian automorphy
items.statement: Continuous p-adic Galois representations have finite dimension over Q_p-bar and are de Rham at all p-adic places. Potentially abelian means that restriction to some finite Galois extension has abelian image; finite up to twist means a character twist has finite image. An irreducible de Rham potentially abelian GL2 representation over a number field is either finite up to twist or the cuspidal automorphic induction of an algebraic Hecke character.

items.name: Odd potentially abelian symplectic automorphy
items.statement: Continuous p-adic Galois representations have finite dimension over Q_p-bar and are de Rham at all p-adic places. Potentially abelian means that restriction to some finite Galois extension has abelian image; finite up to twist means a character twist has finite image. An irreducible de Rham ρ:G_Q→GSp4(Q_p-bar), potentially abelian over a finite Galois extension, with ν(c)=−1 and not finite up to twist, is automorphic. The proof uses the character-orbit cases, automorphic induction and the known odd two-dimensional Artin theorem.

items.name: Reducible compatible-system cases
items.statement: Continuous p-adic Galois representations have finite dimension over Q_p-bar and are de Rham at all p-adic places. Potentially abelian means that restriction to some finite Galois extension has abelian image; finite up to twist means a character twist has finite image. For the source reducible endomorphism types, decompose the compatible system into odd regular rank-two systems or their finite-character inductions and apply the rank-two modularity and automorphic-induction inputs, obtaining isobaric rather than necessarily cuspidal GL4 automorphy.

items.name: Ordinary dyadic torsion lifting target
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite K/Q₂ with residue field F. Let G₁/O be finite flat, killed by2, of rank16 and supplied with λ:G₁≅G₁∨ satisfying λ∨=−λ. Suppose an ordinary PPAV surface A₀/F has A₀[2]≅G₁ special fibre. At2 a skew self-duality is not by itself a strongly alternating polarization datum. The source asserts that A₀ lifts to a PPAV A/O with A[2]≅G₁ (correcting the printed A[p]). It does not explicitly require that the supplied λ be induced by the polarization of A. The proof needs the ordinary polarized-extension argument recorded below; do not strengthen the conclusion to compatibility with an arbitrary λ.

items.name: Symmetric ordinary extension classes
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite K/Q₂ with residue field F. Let G₁/O be finite flat, killed by2, of rank16 and supplied with λ:G₁≅G₁∨ satisfying λ∨=−λ. Suppose an ordinary PPAV surface A₀/F has A₀[2]≅G₁ special fibre. At2 a skew self-duality is not by itself a strongly alternating polarization datum. For the unramified étale lattice V and its dual W, let S(W)⊂W⊗W be generated by x⊗x; use0→S(W)→W⊗W→Λ²W→0 and finite-flat H¹ with Tate twist to describe ordinary extensions.

items.name: Integral local-duality obstruction
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite K/Q₂ with residue field F. Let G₁/O be finite flat, killed by2, of rank16 and supplied with λ:G₁≅G₁∨ satisfying λ∨=−λ. Suppose an ordinary PPAV surface A₀/F has A₀[2]≅G₁ special fibre. At2 a skew self-duality is not by itself a strongly alternating polarization datum. The source claim that nonunit Frobenius eigenvalue1 exclusion forces integral H²(K,M(1))=0 is false. For the ordinary elliptic unit root α of X²+X+2 and M of unramified eigenvalue α², α²≠1 but v₂(α²−1)=3, giving nonzero order8 dual invariants and integral H².

items.name: Finite-flat replacement for the integral obstruction argument
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite K/Q₂ with residue field F. Let G₁/O be finite flat, killed by2, of rank16 and supplied with λ:G₁≅G₁∨ satisfying λ∨=−λ. Suppose an ordinary PPAV surface A₀/F has A₀[2]≅G₁ special fibre. At2 a skew self-duality is not by itself a strongly alternating polarization datum. Kisin09 Lemma2.4.2 gives right exactness of H¹_f(G_K,M(ε)) on discrete unramified p-primary modules, also at2. Apply it to the finite quotients of S(W),W⊗W,Λ²W, then prove compatible inverse-limit lifting through the finite Mittag–Leffler systems. The geometric polarized-extension interpretation remains a separate obligation.

items.name: Skew self-duality does not imply alternation
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite K/Q₂ with residue field F. Let G₁/O be finite flat, killed by2, of rank16 and supplied with λ:G₁≅G₁∨ satisfying λ∨=−λ. Suppose an ordinary PPAV surface A₀/F has A₀[2]≅G₁ special fibre. At2 a skew self-duality is not by itself a strongly alternating polarization datum. On split μ₂²⊕(Z/2)² over Z₂, the perfect pairing with matrix [[0,I],[I,diag(1,0)]] is skew self-dual in characteristic2 and has isotropic connected part, but is not alternating on the generic fibre. This refutes the explanatory shortcut, not the possibility of lifting the underlying split group with another polarization.

items.name: Ordinary polarized deformation approach
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite K/Q₂ with residue field F. Let G₁/O be finite flat, killed by2, of rank16 and supplied with λ:G₁≅G₁∨ satisfying λ∨=−λ. Suppose an ordinary PPAV surface A₀/F has A₀[2]≅G₁ special fibre. At2 a skew self-duality is not by itself a strongly alternating polarization datum. Construct the ordinary polarized Serre–Tate formal torus of dimension3, identify its finite2-torsion extension classes and the finite Frobenius-descent action, and prove the lifting statement by formal smoothness and compatible descent. This is a precise repair obligation, not a proof already carried out in the source audit.

items.name: Rational sextic parameter space for fixed mod2 image
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→Sp4(F2)=S6 be continuous and unramified at3, with nonidentity Frobenius at3. Assume a specified ordinary finite flat model W/Z₂ of ρ̄ exists and is isomorphic to its Cartier dual; ordinary means an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative group. The specified model, not only the generic representation, is part of the hypothesis. Let K be the degree-six étale algebra of ρ̄. In its six-dimensional affine space take primitive elements θ with separable degree-six characteristic polynomial of multiplication. Their sextics y²=f_θ(x) have Jacobian2-torsion ρ̄; projective homogenization must retain the valid affine chart and exclude the discriminant locus.

items.name: Nontrivial Frobenius partitions at three
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→Sp4(F2)=S6 be continuous and unramified at3, with nonidentity Frobenius at3. Assume a specified ordinary finite flat model W/Z₂ of ρ̄ exists and is isomorphic to its Cartier dual; ordinary means an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative group. The specified model, not only the generic representation, is part of the hypothesis. Construct local ordinary distinguished PPAV seeds for the ten nonidentity partitions of6. Nine listed p220 curve rows have the stated distinction; the[2,2,2] row f=x⁶+4x⁴+6x³−8x²+1 has Q₃=(X²+2X+3)² and fails. Its replacement is the separately specified Weil restriction seed.

items.name: Weil-restriction seed for three transpositions
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→Sp4(F2)=S6 be continuous and unramified at3, with nonidentity Frobenius at3. Assume a specified ordinary finite flat model W/Z₂ of ρ̄ exists and is isomorphic to its Cartier dual; ordinary means an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative group. The specified model, not only the generic representation, is part of the hypothesis. Over F9=F3[t]/(t²+1), take E:y²=x(x−1)(x−t), with #E(F9)=8 and full rational2-torsion. Res_{F9/F3}E has the descended product principal polarization, Q₃=X⁴−2X²+9 and Frobenius2-torsion type[2,2,2]. Lift and use polarized deformation, the Torelli open locus and local constancy to obtain a Q₃ Jacobian; the finite calculations are verified, the geometric bridge is a proof obligation.

items.name: Three ordinary étale-two special fibres
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→Sp4(F2)=S6 be continuous and unramified at3, with nonidentity Frobenius at3. Assume a specified ordinary finite flat model W/Z₂ of ρ̄ exists and is isomorphic to its Cartier dual; ordinary means an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative group. The specified model, not only the generic representation, is part of the hypothesis. The three source F2 curves realize the possible order1,2,3 Frobenius actions on the rank2 étale quotient of W, with ordinary quartics avoiding the two excluded mod3 polynomials. In the middle case Q₂=X⁴+2X³+3X²+4X+4 and #Jac(F2)=14 distinguish the nontrivial Jordan quotient.

items.name: Global ordinary mod2 realization target
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→Sp4(F2)=S6 be continuous and unramified at3, with nonidentity Frobenius at3. Assume a specified ordinary finite flat model W/Z₂ of ρ̄ exists and is isomorphic to its Cartier dual; ordinary means an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative group. The specified model, not only the generic representation, is part of the hypothesis. Using the dyadic polarized lifting and corrected local3 table, the source target is A/Q with good ordinary reduction at2,3,3-distinction, A[2]/Z₂≅W, full mod3 image, mod2 image ρ̄ and Q₂ not congruent to X⁴±X³+2X²∓X+1 mod3. Rational sextic approximation and thin-set avoidance finish only after the local polarized/geometric repair obligations.

items.name: Identity Frobenius obstruction to the local seed
items.statement: For a smooth good-reduction genus-two curve over Q₃, trivial Frobenius on its2-torsion would give six distinct F3-rational Weierstrass points on P1, impossible since #P1(F3)=4. A product of elliptic curves over F3 with full rational2-torsion also fails as an ordinary seed: Hasse forces each elliptic curve to have4 points and trace0, hence be supersingular. The source does not prove impossibility for every other possible special-fibre construction.

items.name: Ordinary mod2 modularity target
items.statement: Let ρ̄:G_Q→Sp4(F2)=S6 be continuous and unramified at3, with nonidentity Frobenius at3. Assume a specified ordinary finite flat model W/Z₂ of ρ̄ exists and is isomorphic to its Cartier dual; ordinary means an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative group. The specified model, not only the generic representation, is part of the hypothesis. Under the stated ordinary Cartier-self-dual model and nontrivial unramified Frobenius3 hypotheses, the source concludes that ρ̄ is ordinarily modular of weight2 and level prime to6 by applying the main theorem to10.3.6. This endpoint retains its local lifting/table repair gates.

items.name: Finite flat generic image is insufficient
items.statement: Over Q₂ an unramified four-dimensional F2 representation with image of order5 is generically finite flat (and ordinary in the residual-character sense), but its finite-flat models over Z₂ are étale or multiplicative, hence not Cartier self-dual and cannot be A[2] for an abelian surface with good reduction. Generic finite-flatness therefore does not replace the specified ordinary self-dual model in10.3.9. For p>2 finite-flat models over Z_p are determined by their generic fibre in this setting.

items.name: Regular-weight Serre implies abelian-surface modularity
items.statement: Use the source regular-weight residual Serre assertion: for every relevant prime p and every absolutely irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p) of multiplier ε̄⁻¹ whose local-p semisimplification is a sum of characters, there is an ordinary cuspidal GSp4/Q form of REGULAR weight, level prime to p and central character absolute-value squared with residual representation ρ̄. Assuming this residual Serre assertion, every abelian surface A/Q is modular in the isobaric sense of1.8.25. Reduce the32 established types, choose ordinary distinguished sufficiently large p with the required residual image for typesA and B[C₂], and use the ordinary component and nonregular lifting theorem.

items.name: Sufficiently large primes suffice
items.statement: Use the source regular-weight residual Serre assertion: for every relevant prime p and every absolutely irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p) of multiplier ε̄⁻¹ whose local-p semisimplification is a sum of characters, there is an ordinary cuspidal GSp4/Q form of REGULAR weight, level prime to p and central character absolute-value squared with residual representation ρ̄. The same implication holds if the regular-weight Serre assertion is assumed only for sufficiently large primes, because the ordinary/distinguished/image conditions are obtained on a density-one set with the additional endomorphism-field splitting conditions.

items.name: Relative abelian scheme
items.statement: These are prerequisites imported by the BCGP25 programme (especially §§1.6,4–7,9–10) from existing atlas owners, including the ten-author infrastructure arXiv1812.09999. Import the relative carrier, not only the existing field-valued abelian variety.

items.statement: Let O be the p-adic coefficient DVR with residue field k, and Λ a complete Noetherian local O-algebra with residue field k. CNL_Λ has complete Noetherian local Λ-algebras A with residue field identified with k, and continuous local Λ-morphisms inducing the specified residue map.

items.name: Local finite-level VB presentations
items.statement: For a Hodge-type tower with fixed toroidal cone data Σ, choose an open flag neighborhood U_FL and its tower preimage U_{K^p,Σ}. Let F be an LB g-sheaf; VB_Σ(F)=colim_{K′_p}RΓ(K′_p,π_HT,Σ⁻¹F⊗^L_{π_HT,Σ⁻¹O_FL}O_U). If the moving nilradical annihilates F, then on an affinoid cover VB_Σ⁰(F) is a colimit of base changes of finite-level summands of orthonormalizable Banach sheaves, and tensoring it from O^sm to O_U gives the underived Hodge–Tate pullback of F.

items.name: Exact local VB descent

items.statement: For a Hodge-type tower with fixed toroidal cone data Σ, choose an open flag neighborhood U_FL and its tower preimage U_{K^p,Σ}. items.statement: For a Hodge-type tower with fixed toroidal cone data Σ, choose an open flag neighborhood U_FL and its tower preimage U_{K^p,Σ}. This is the locally analytic form of4.4.1, separate from its unrestricted primitive comparison.

items.name: Arithmetic Sen functor
items.statement: For a Hodge-type tower with fixed toroidal cone data Σ, choose an open flag neighborhood U_FL and its tower preimage U_{K^p,Σ}. Let F be an LB g-sheaf; VB_Σ(F)=colim_{K′_p}RΓ(K′_p,π_HT,Σ⁻¹F⊗^L_{π_HT,Σ⁻¹O_FL}O_U). For a continuous semilinear Galois sheaf F on the tower, S^arit(F) is the colimit over finite E′/E of the G_{E′_cycl}-fixed vectors that are analytic for Gal(E′_cycl/E'); differentiate the cyclotomic action to define its O^{sm,Galois-sm}-linear Sen operator.

items.name: Solvable CM descent to GSp4
items.statement: Let ρ:G_Q→GSp4(Q_p-bar) be continuous with multiplier ε⁻¹. Galois representations of RACSDC GL4 forms use the r_π normalization; GSp4 forms use ρ_π. If F/Q is solvable Galois and CM, ρ restricted to G_F is irreducible, and a RACSDC GL4/F form π_F satisfies ρ restricted to G_F≅r_{π_F,p}⊗ε, then ρ comes from a regular algebraic cuspidal GSp4/Q form with central character absolute-value squared.

items.name: Solvable totally real descent to GSp4
items.statement: Let ρ:G_Q→GSp4(Q_p-bar) be continuous with multiplier ε⁻¹. Galois representations of RACSDC GL4 forms use the r_π normalization; GSp4 forms use ρ_π. If F⁺/Q is solvable Galois and totally real, ρ restricted to G_F⁺ is irreducible and equals ρ_{π_F⁺,p} for a regular algebraic cuspidal GSp4/F⁺ form with central character absolute-value squared, then ρ comes from such a GSp4/Q form.

items.name: Coalgebra comodule carrier
items.statement: The following declaration statements were read at TauCeti f790474 in Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean and Cat.lean. TauCeti.Comodule R C M is a right coaction M→M⊗_R C with coassociativity and counit; ComoduleCat bundles these over a commutative semiring. This already supplies the algebraic carrier, but a left-coaction/action convention adapter and analytic/solid coefficient structures are separate.
